Repo /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper, trail #369 slice 4 (owner decision 2026-11-12: the Go typescript beta stays ONLY as the oracle/goldens/parity gate in apps/oracle; the product uses the published tsrs crates in process). Branch from origin/main as `feat/delete-process-route` (main = 7e024e25: checker default (#441), extract speed (#443/#444), in-process checker (#438)). Read docs/adr/0026-the-checker-is-the-type-authority.md (slice plan, "Spawn the tsrs binary" alternative, risks), trail #369 body (`entire trail show 369 --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper --project gh/orin-dx`: slice 4 and 5 text), docs/type-checker-integration.md, crates/semantic/src/{checker.rs,rpc.rs,locate.rs,lib.rs,on_demand.rs}, crates/tsc-client, apps/oracle/package.json, scripts/check-packaging.mjs, .github/workflows/ci.yml (CALIPER_TEST_TSC lines).
Deliver: (1) Delete the product's process route: the process Client variant under rpc.rs and its supervision/restart code in the product path, `Backend::start` path argument and `--tsc-path`/`tscPath` options (CLI, config, napi, Storybook addon, docs, help trycmd, changeset with Breaking:/Action: note; one name per concept; no new option), `crates/semantic/src/locate.rs` (binary discovery, @tsrs/<platform> mapping, version recognition in lib.rs), the project-`typescript@7.1.0-beta` fallback (trail #368), `examples/record_fixture.rs` process-route bits if dead, packaging remnants. (2) `crates/tsc-client`: decide with evidence whether anything still needs it. The Rust tests that used the Go beta over a pipe (CALIPER_TEST_TSC, replay fixtures recorded with the Go checker) either move to the built-in checker with re-recorded fixtures (preferred: record with tsrs; Go parity is already covered by `construct:parity`) or, only if a test genuinely needs the Go checker, keep tsc-client as a dev-dependency/test-only crate (not published, not a product dependency). If tsc-client can be deleted entirely (workspace member, changeset/CHANGELOG, deny/semver config, CI references), delete it. Keep apps/oracle `typescript-beta` and its construct goldens + construct:parity untouched. (3) CI: remove CALIPER_TEST_TSC wiring from ci.yml where no longer needed; make scripts/check-packaging.mjs assert the oracle's npm `tsrs` pin equals the Cargo `=` pin of tsrs_api/tsrs_vfs (slice 5 item) if the repo already has a packaging check that can host it, otherwise skip and say so; dependabot ignore list for tsrs crates if not present (slice 5). (4) Docs: ADR 0026 slice markers (S4 packaging/process route deleted; the 'Spawn the tsrs binary' alternative stays as rejected), type-checker-integration.md, STATUS, READMEs, option docs; delete dead docs about the process route. (5) Delete what the change makes dead in the same PR (no stragglers); run `just machete`; `cargo deny`, `just semver` (public API removals need the right bump: tsc-client or semantic public items; changesets).
Overlap: PR #440 (feat/in-process-guards, being merged by another worker) edits checker.rs, on_demand.rs, rpc.rs (guards: memory bound, panic recovery, snapshot release on refusal). Do not rewrite those files beyond the deletions you need; keep hunks small; before your FINAL push, `git fetch origin` and merge origin/main (merge commit, no rebase/force-push) which may by then contain #440, resolving conflicts keeping #440's guards on the in-process path.
Rules: scratch in ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/slice-4/ (no /tmp); NO oracle runs, no corpus fetches; no new scripts/options/recipes; do not run benchmarks in parallel with other jobs (just identity/tests). Rust 1.99.1 toolchain first on PATH (/Users/gabe/.rustup/toolchains/1.99.1-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin; mise forces 1.98.1), outside the sandbox where tests need it, `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile` in the worktree if needed. Before push: `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `just deny`, `just semver`, `just test-rust`, `just test-checker-lane`, `just test-ts`, `just test-napi`, `just test-integration`, `construct:parity` (free), and a full-content diff of `extract --json` before/after on ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large/src (byte-identical apart from stats); judge each by exit code. Signed commits with trailer `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013R2ytvK9B32ZaSUaSe6aAZ`. The Entire pre-push hook is fixed: push normally with `git push origin HEAD:feat/delete-process-route`, NEVER --no-verify, and verify with `git ls-remote origin feat/delete-process-route` that the remote SHA equals your HEAD. Do not open the PR (the lead links it), do not poll CI. Final report (<= 300 words): what was deleted (files/LOC), what tests moved and how, public-API/semver and changeset notes, what remains of Go beta (oracle only) and of tsc-client, checks run with exit codes, SHAs, what was not verified.

<system-reminder>
Your final report is delivered through SubagentHandback: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so make it your last step. Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered. Do not also send the report with SendMessage: your caller would get it twice.

Trail #369: spike: use the published tsrs crates in-process instead of spawning the tsrs binary
  ID:            01M76QSVR5V2D9M975C1V87NYW
  Project:       gh/orin-dx
  Status:        open
  Phase:         building
  URL:           https://entire.com/gh/orin-dx/-/trails/369
  Assignees:     ulid:01KY3576VGXBH5688NK9BQNC88
  Type:          task
  Priority:      high
  Created:       2026-11-12T02:01:19Z
  Last activity: 2026-11-13T06:40:47Z
  Changes:
    CHANGE       BRANCH                  BASE  STATUS  URL
    caliper/236                          main  merged  https://entire.com/gh/orin-dx/-/trails/369/changes/caliper/236
    caliper/238  feat/in-process-guards  main  open    https://entire.com/gh/orin-dx/-/trails/369/changes/caliper/238
  Gates for caliper/238:
    Mergeable: no
    Head:      10df5137
    Conflicts: conflicting
    Gates:
      ✗ approvals   failed   No reviewers have approved this trail
      ✓ checks      passed   CI checks have passed
      ✓ findings    passed   No blocking findings
      - up_to_date  skipped  14 commits behind (non-blocking)
    Checks:    19 passed · 0 running · 0 failed (19 total)

Description:
Intent: tsrs_api 0.24.0 and tsrs_core 0.24.0 are on crates.io (Apache-2.0, oxc-project/tsrs, rust-version 1.99). The spike (2026-11-12) measured the same recorded ChakraButton answer (3,776 requests) at 141 ms in-process against 367 ms over the pipe (0.23 binary): the cost is the pipe, not the checker; answers are equal; all 34 methods the converter sends exist in tsrs_api::Session (Handler::handle_request(method, params_json)). 0.23, 0.24 and 0.25 all target TypeScript 3e9236361fa9; only 0.24.0 is published. DECISION: adopt, in slices, behind the existing opt-in; the Go typescript beta stays as the oracle and the parity gate. Slices (all link to this trail): (1) in-process transport: tsrs_api and tsrs_vfs pinned =0.24.0, one checker thread with a 512 MiB stack owning the Session, a channel replaces the pipe, --tsc-path keeps the process route (Go checker in tests); cargo deny allows BSL-1.0 and Unicode-DFS-2016, NOTICE ships; gates: lint, replay tests, checker lane unchanged, byte-identical whole-program output on gate-large, first answer over 9 interleaved runs. (2) memory and abort guards: drop the session on the 64-program and RSS rules, past the bound answer structurally with a diagnostic; deep-type test at 10,000; panic is never abort; memory, watch and determinism gates re-run in-process. (3) napi default for the opt-in: a Node integration test, a panic hook, peak RSS recorded. (4) delete the product process route: tsc-client becomes test-only for Go, @tsrs/<platform> packaging (PR 434) and locate.rs gone, check-packaging compares the oracle's tsrs npm pin with the Cargo pin; the project-typescript-beta fallback (trail 368) goes with it. (5) pin-bump procedure: construct:parity with the npm tsrs matching the crate version; tsrs crates added to the dependabot ignore list. Risks: a stack overflow aborts the host process (uncatchable; the binary serves on 512 MiB threads: 2,000-deep types abort a 2 MiB thread); dropping a session does not return memory (+146 MiB over 60 programs, so the 64-program and 768 MiB reset is lost in-process); about 20 MB per linked artifact; tsrs_core pins unicode-id-start =1.1.2 (forces oxc's copy down from 1.5.0). Ask upstream: publish crates with every tag (0.25 is missing), relax the =1.1.2 pin, a stack guard that turns overflow into an error, an arena trim or reset, document embedder stack requirements. Source: crates spike report; owner direction 2026-11-12.

[workspace]
members = [
    "crates/core",
    "crates/binding",
    "crates/cli",
    "crates/tsc-client",
    "crates/semantic",
]
resolver = "2"

[workspace.package]
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.99"
authors = ["caliper-docgen contributors"]
license = "FSL-1.1-MIT"
repository = "https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper"
homepage = "https://orin-dx.com/tools/caliper/"
keywords = ["react", "docgen", "typescript", "oxc", "storybook"]
categories = ["development-tools", "command-line-utilities"]

# "deny" rather than "forbid": a member crate could locally #[allow(unsafe_code)]
# on a real FFI boundary if one ever needs it — none currently do (verified:
# zero `unsafe` usage across crates/core, crates/cli, crates/binding; napi-rs's
# #[napi] macros generate the FFI glue without user-visible unsafe).
[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "deny"
unused_must_use = "deny"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
unwrap_used = "deny"
expect_used = "deny"
panic = "deny"
dbg_macro = "deny"
# Only `main` ends the process, so a command's exit decision stays testable; the one other exit is allowed in place.
exit = "deny"
print_stdout = "deny"
print_stderr = "deny"
map_err_ignore = "deny"
let_underscore_must_use = "deny"

[workspace.dependencies]
# OXC — all main crates move in lockstep; resolver has separate versioning
oxc_allocator     = "0.157"
oxc_parser        = "0.157"
oxc_ast           = "0.157"
oxc_ast_visit     = "0.157"
oxc_span          = "0.157"
oxc_str           = "0.157"
oxc_syntax        = "0.157"
oxc_resolver      = "11"

# The TypeScript checker the semantic backend links (ADR 0026). Exact pins: a bump is a parity check against the Go
# checker, never a lockfile refresh.
tsrs_api          = "=0.24.0"
tsrs_vfs          = "=0.24.0"

# Core data
compact_str       = { version = "0.10", features = ["serde"] }
rustc-hash        = "2.1"
dashmap           = "6.1"
arc-swap          = "1.9"
camino            = { version = "1.2", features = ["serde1"] }

# Serde
serde             = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive", "rc"] }
serde_json        = "1.0"
json-strip-comments = "3.1"
rmp-serde         = "1.3"

# Error handling
miette            = "7.6"

# Parallelism
rayon             = "1.12"
mimalloc          = "0.1"
tokio             = { version = "1.52", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "process", "io-util", "sync", "macros"] }

# File system
ignore            = "0.4"

# CLI
clap              = { version = "4.6", features = ["derive", "env", "wrap_help"] }
clap_complete     = "4.6"
indicatif         = "0.18"
tracing           = "0.1"
tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", features = ["env-filter", "fmt"] }
owo-colors        = "4.3"
watchexec         = "8.2"

# NAPI (3.x series)
napi              = { version = "3", features = ["napi4"] }
napi-derive       = "3"

# Dev
criterion         = "0.8"
insta             = { version = "1.48", features = ["json", "redactions"] }
tempfile          = "3.20"
rstest            = "0.28"
trycmd            = "1.2"

[profile.release]
opt-level = 3
lto = "thin"
codegen-units = 1

[profile.bench]
inherits = "release"
debug = true

61:      # The cli config tests spawn `node --import=tsx/esm`, and tsx is a devDependency of apps/oracle.
67:      # The two tests that run the real TypeScript 7.1 checker use apps/oracle's `typescript-beta`; without this they
71:          CALIPER_TEST_TSC: ${{ github.workspace }}/apps/oracle/node_modules/typescript-beta/bin/tsc
73:  # ADR 0026's gates for the checker path: the golden check, tsrs against the Go checker, and the construct suite through
74:  # the checker held to apps/oracle/construct-suite/checker-expectations.json. It builds its own release binary, a second
76:  test-checker-lane:
96:      - run: just test-checker-lane
218:          CALIPER_TEST_TSC: ${{ github.workspace }}/apps/oracle/node_modules/typescript-beta/bin/tsc
329:    needs: [lint, test-rust, test-checker-lane, test-napi, test-py, test-ts, test-integration, test-construct, coverage, install, semver, msrv, audit, changesets]
----
# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install Cargo tools required for local development
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest --locked
    cargo install cargo-llvm-cov --locked
    cargo install cargo-machete --locked
    cargo install cargo-semver-checks --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Check the public Rust API of every published library crate for SemVer breaks against the last published version.
# The version only moves in the release PR, so a break is accepted when a pending minor or major changeset covers the
# crate. The CLI crate is a binary and has no library API.
semver:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -uo pipefail
    status=0
    for crate in caliper-docgen-core caliper-docgen-semantic caliper-docgen-tsc-client; do
        if cargo semver-checks check-release -p "$crate"; then
            continue
        fi
        if grep -qsE "^cargo/$crate: (minor|major)$" .changeset/*.md; then
            echo "breaking API changes are covered by a pending minor or major changeset for $crate"
            continue
        fi
        echo "breaking API changes need a minor or major changeset for cargo/$crate" >&2
        status=1
    done
    exit "$status"

# Build with the minimum supported Rust version declared in Cargo.toml.
msrv:
    cargo +$(sed -n 's/^rust-version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml) check --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked

# Build all projects. Rust crates build via one workspace-wide cargo
# invocation, not `moon run :build` — that fans out one `cargo build -p`
# per crate, and every one of those processes contends for the same
# target/ file lock, serializing what moon's own scheduler thinks is
# parallel work (confirmed via `Blocking waiting for file lock` in verbose
# output). napi/vite-plugin have no such lock to contend over, so moon
# still orchestrates those directly.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi
    moon run napi:build vite-plugin:build
    cargo build --release

# Run all tests (Rust, the native binding crate, TypeScript, Python)
test: test-rust test-napi test-ts test-py

# Run Rust tests (via nextest, which doesn't run doctests — paired
# with `cargo test --doc` to cover those too)
test-rust:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi

# The binding crate is excluded from the workspace recipes, so its own unit tests run here.
test-napi:
    cargo nextest run -p caliper-docgen-napi --locked

# Run the Python tests for the scripts (standard library only, no dependencies)
test-py:
    python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'

# Run TypeScript tests
test-ts:
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-storybook test
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle test

# Compare the Go checker and tsrs on every construct-suite row (run on every tsrs bump; see apps/oracle/construct-suite/README.md)
test-parity:
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:parity

# The checker gates of ADR 0026, with nothing allowed to skip: the golden check, tsrs-against-Go parity, and the construct
# suite through the checker path held to checker-expectations.json. The pinned tsrs binary is the one the `tsrs` package
# itself selects for this platform (@tsrs/<os>-<arch>[-gnu|-musl]); see apps/oracle/construct-suite/README.md.
test-checker-lane:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen
    export REQUIRE_TSRS=1 REQUIRE_CALIPER_BIN=1 CALIPER_BIN="$PWD/target/release/caliper-docgen"
    TSRS_BIN="$(pnpm --silent --filter caliper-docgen-oracle exec tsx src/tsrs-bin.ts)"
    export TSRS_BIN
    echo "tsrs: $TSRS_BIN"
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:check
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:parity
    CALIPER_SEMANTIC=1 pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:checker
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle exec vitest run tests/construct-checker-lane.test.ts
    # S5's gate on tsrs: generic components instantiated (Test / Rust runs the same tests on the Go checker).
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --lib instantiate
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --test instantiate
    # S6's gate on tsrs: a kept snapshot brought up to date, and an edit nobody announced caught loudly.
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --test watch

# Build the native binding and run the Vite plugin against it
test-integration:
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-napi build:napi
    NAPI_BINARY_REQUIRED=true pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test:integration
    NAPI_BINARY_REQUIRED=true pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-storybook test:integration

# Measure ADR 0026's memory, determinism, first-answer and watch gates against the pinned tsrs
# (docs/gate-measurements.md). Builds the large project outside the repository (GATE_FIXTURES, default
# ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large), so it needs the network or a warm pnpm store; `just gate-measure --runs 3`
# passes options to every gate. Takes minutes, runs every gate, and fails if any failed.
gate-measure *args:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    fixtures="${GATE_FIXTURES:-$HOME/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large}"
    node scripts/gate_fixtures.mjs "$fixtures"
    cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --example gate_harness
    TSRS_BIN="$(pnpm --silent --filter caliper-docgen-oracle exec tsx src/tsrs-bin.ts)"
    failed=0
    for gate in memory determinism first-answer watch; do
        target/release/examples/gate_harness "$gate" --src "$fixtures/src" --tsc "$TSRS_BIN" {{ args }} || failed=1
    done
    exit "$failed"

# The deterministic construct suite on the release binary: goldens current, then the suite, which must not skip
test-construct:
    cargo build --release -p caliper-docgen --locked
    CALIPER_BIN="$PWD/target/release/caliper-docgen" pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:check
    CALIPER_BIN="$PWD/target/release/caliper-docgen" REQUIRE_CALIPER_BIN=1 pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle test

# Pack the npm packages and check napi arrives only as vite-plugin's transitive dependency (pm: npm or pnpm)
verify-install pm="pnpm":
    scripts/verify-install.sh {{ pm }}

# Rust and TypeScript line coverage; with a threshold, fails if either is below it
coverage threshold="": (coverage-rust threshold) (coverage-ts threshold)

# Rust coverage: writes lcov.info and prints the summary before enforcing the threshold
coverage-rust threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked --lcov --output-path lcov.info
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{ threshold }}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{ threshold }}"
    fi

# TypeScript coverage: prints the summaries and writes each package's coverage/lcov.info
coverage-ts threshold="":
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin exec vitest run --coverage {{ if threshold != "" { "--coverage.thresholds.lines=" + threshold } else { "" } }}
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-storybook exec vitest run --coverage {{ if threshold != "" { "--coverage.thresholds.lines=" + threshold } else { "" } }}

# Documentation build check (warnings, including broken intra-doc links,
# treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi

# Unused-dependency check
machete:
    cargo machete

ts_src := "'packages/vite-plugin/src/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/tests/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/storybook/src/**/*.ts' 'packages/storybook/tests/**/*.ts' 'packages/storybook/*.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/oracle/src/**/*.ts' 'apps/oracle/tests/**/*.ts'"
ts_src_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/src' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/storybook/src' 'packages/storybook/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/oracle/src'"
ts_tests_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/tests' 'packages/storybook/tests' 'apps/oracle/tests'"
md_src := "'**/*.md' '!node_modules/**' '!target/**' '!dist/**'"

# Lint and format check

----
# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install Cargo tools required for local development
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest --locked
    cargo install cargo-llvm-cov --locked
    cargo install cargo-machete --locked
    cargo install cargo-semver-checks --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Check the public Rust API of every published library crate for SemVer breaks against the last published version.
# The version only moves in the release PR, so a break is accepted when a pending minor or major changeset covers the
# crate. The CLI crate is a binary and has no library API.
semver:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -uo pipefail
    status=0
    for crate in caliper-docgen-core caliper-docgen-semantic caliper-docgen-tsc-client; do
        if cargo semver-checks check-release -p "$crate"; then
            continue
        fi
        if grep -qsE "^cargo/$crate: (minor|major)$" .changeset/*.md; then
            echo "breaking API changes are covered by a pending minor or major changeset for $crate"
            continue
        fi
        echo "breaking API changes need a minor or major changeset for cargo/$crate" >&2
        status=1
    done
    exit "$status"

# Build with the minimum supported Rust version declared in Cargo.toml.
msrv:
    cargo +$(sed -n 's/^rust-version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml) check --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked

# Build all projects. Rust crates build via one workspace-wide cargo
# invocation, not `moon run :build` — that fans out one `cargo build -p`
# per crate, and every one of those processes contends for the same
# target/ file lock, serializing what moon's own scheduler thinks is
# parallel work (confirmed via `Blocking waiting for file lock` in verbose
# output). napi/vite-plugin have no such lock to contend over, so moon
# still orchestrates those directly.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi
    moon run napi:build vite-plugin:build
    cargo build --release

# Run all tests (Rust, the native binding crate, TypeScript, Python)
test: test-rust test-napi test-ts test-py

# Run Rust tests (via nextest, which doesn't run doctests — paired
# with `cargo test --doc` to cover those too)
test-rust:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi

# The binding crate is excluded from the workspace recipes, so its own unit tests run here.
test-napi:
    cargo nextest run -p caliper-docgen-napi --locked

# Run the Python tests for the scripts (standard library only, no dependencies)
test-py:
    python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'

# Run TypeScript tests
test-ts:
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-storybook test
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle test

# Compare the Go checker and tsrs on every construct-suite row (run on every tsrs bump; see apps/oracle/construct-suite/README.md)
test-parity:
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:parity

# The checker gates of ADR 0026, with nothing allowed to skip: the golden check, tsrs-against-Go parity, and the construct
# suite through the checker path held to checker-expectations.json. The pinned tsrs binary is the one the `tsrs` package
# itself selects for this platform (@tsrs/<os>-<arch>[-gnu|-musl]); see apps/oracle/construct-suite/README.md.
test-checker-lane:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen
    export REQUIRE_TSRS=1 REQUIRE_CALIPER_BIN=1 CALIPER_BIN="$PWD/target/release/caliper-docgen"
    TSRS_BIN="$(pnpm --silent --filter caliper-docgen-oracle exec tsx src/tsrs-bin.ts)"
    export TSRS_BIN
    echo "tsrs: $TSRS_BIN"
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:check
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:parity
    CALIPER_SEMANTIC=1 pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:checker
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle exec vitest run tests/construct-checker-lane.test.ts
    # S5's gate on tsrs: generic components instantiated (Test / Rust runs the same tests on the Go checker).
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --lib instantiate
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --test instantiate
    # S6's gate on tsrs: a kept snapshot brought up to date, and an edit nobody announced caught loudly.
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --test watch

# Build the native binding and run the Vite plugin against it
test-integration:
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-napi build:napi
    NAPI_BINARY_REQUIRED=true pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test:integration
    NAPI_BINARY_REQUIRED=true pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-storybook test:integration

# Measure ADR 0026's memory, determinism, first-answer and watch gates against the pinned tsrs
# (docs/gate-measurements.md). Builds the large project outside the repository (GATE_FIXTURES, default
# ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large), so it needs the network or a warm pnpm store; `just gate-measure --runs 3`
# passes options to every gate. Takes minutes, runs every gate, and fails if any failed.
gate-measure *args:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    fixtures="${GATE_FIXTURES:-$HOME/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large}"
    node scripts/gate_fixtures.mjs "$fixtures"
    cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --example gate_harness
    TSRS_BIN="$(pnpm --silent --filter caliper-docgen-oracle exec tsx src/tsrs-bin.ts)"
    failed=0
    for gate in memory determinism first-answer watch; do
        target/release/examples/gate_harness "$gate" --src "$fixtures/src" --tsc "$TSRS_BIN" {{ args }} || failed=1
    done
    exit "$failed"

# The deterministic construct suite on the release binary: goldens current, then the suite, which must not skip
test-construct:
    cargo build --release -p caliper-docgen --locked
    CALIPER_BIN="$PWD/target/release/caliper-docgen" pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:check
    CALIPER_BIN="$PWD/target/release/caliper-docgen" REQUIRE_CALIPER_BIN=1 pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle test

# Pack the npm packages and check napi arrives only as vite-plugin's transitive dependency (pm: npm or pnpm)
verify-install pm="pnpm":
    scripts/verify-install.sh {{ pm }}

# Rust and TypeScript line coverage; with a threshold, fails if either is below it
coverage threshold="": (coverage-rust threshold) (coverage-ts threshold)

# Rust coverage: writes lcov.info and prints the summary before enforcing the threshold
coverage-rust threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked --lcov --output-path lcov.info
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{ threshold }}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{ threshold }}"
    fi

# TypeScript coverage: prints the summaries and writes each package's coverage/lcov.info
coverage-ts threshold="":
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin exec vitest run --coverage {{ if threshold != "" { "--coverage.thresholds.lines=" + threshold } else { "" } }}
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-storybook exec vitest run --coverage {{ if threshold != "" { "--coverage.thresholds.lines=" + threshold } else { "" } }}

# Documentation build check (warnings, including broken intra-doc links,

doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi

# Unused-dependency check
machete:

# Dependency updates. Every ecosystem is grouped into a single routine PR per
# week so the queue stays reviewable, with security updates kept in their own
# group so an advisory fix is never hidden inside a large routine bump.
#
# `cooldown` deliberately lags fresh releases: this repo pins GitHub Actions
# by commit SHA, and a week is long enough for a yanked crate or a pulled
# action release to surface before it lands in a PR here.
version: 2

updates:
  - package-ecosystem: github-actions
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7
    open-pull-requests-limit: 3
    groups:
      routine-actions:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["*"]
      security-actions:
        applies-to: security-updates
        patterns: ["*"]

  - package-ecosystem: cargo
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
    groups:
      # oxc_resolver is versioned separately from the lockstep oxc_* crates, so it gets its own PR.
      oxc-resolver:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["oxc_resolver"]
      # The oxc_* crates are released in lockstep and their minor releases
      # carry breaking API changes; keeping them in one PR means the
      # extractor and resolver are updated together or not at all.
      oxc:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["oxc_*"]
        exclude-patterns: ["oxc_resolver"]
      routine-cargo:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["*"]
        exclude-patterns: ["oxc_*"]
      security-cargo:
        applies-to: security-updates
        patterns: ["*"]

  - package-ecosystem: npm
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7
    open-pull-requests-limit: 3
    groups:
      routine-npm:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["*"]
      security-npm:
        applies-to: security-updates
        patterns: ["*"]
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@b80e2bb2635f28eb98b9fce1e2f0887e1535c6b2 # v2.90.0
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-nextest
      # The cli config tests spawn `node --import=tsx/esm`, and tsx is a devDependency of apps/oracle.
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0.6.4
        with:
          auto-install: true
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-pnpm-cache@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      # The two tests that run the real TypeScript 7.1 checker use apps/oracle's `typescript-beta`; without this they
      # skip, and in CI a skip is a failure.
      - run: just test-rust
        env:
          CALIPER_TEST_TSC: ${{ github.workspace }}/apps/oracle/node_modules/typescript-beta/bin/tsc

  # ADR 0026's gates for the checker path: the golden check, tsrs against the Go checker, and the construct suite through
  # the checker held to apps/oracle/construct-suite/checker-expectations.json. It builds its own release binary, a second
  # build beside the other jobs (setup-rust caches cargo); nothing may skip.
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@b80e2bb2635f28eb98b9fce1e2f0887e1535c6b2 # v2.90.0
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-nextest,cargo-llvm-cov
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0.6.4
        with:
          auto-install: true
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-pnpm-cache@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      # Same as `test-rust`: the real-checker tests fail without it on CI, and they count towards coverage.
      - run: just coverage 90
        env:
          CALIPER_TEST_TSC: ${{ github.workspace }}/apps/oracle/node_modules/typescript-beta/bin/tsc
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always()
        with:
          name: coverage
          path: |
            lcov.info
            packages/vite-plugin/coverage/lcov.info

crates/binding/CHANGELOG.md:5:- `export const Button = InternalButton` and `memo(InternalButton)` are components even when `InternalButton` is declared further down the file; the alias used to be dropped, and reported as a skipped candidate, whenever it came first.
crates/binding/CHANGELOG.md:15:- `Root.Item = memo(...)` and `Root.Item = forwardRef(...)` now leave a skip note saying the sub-component is not read, instead of vanishing from the output without a word. Other assigned calls, such as `Root.Context = createContext(...)`, stay silent because they are not components.
crates/binding/CHANGELOG.md:17:- A constant such as `MENU_OPTIONS` or `ORIGIN` is no longer reported as a skipped component candidate: on shadcn/ui and Ant Design that removes 211 of the 398 skip notes (163 of 252 and 48 of 146), with the extracted components unchanged.
crates/binding/CHANGELOG.md:18:- A dependency declaration file that exists but cannot be read (bad permissions, invalid UTF-8) is now reported as an `IoError` warning naming the file, instead of being skipped without a word, which left the types it declares missing with no explanation. Concurrent runs also no longer share one temporary file when saving the dependency type index.
crates/binding/CHANGELOG.md:22:- A component built by calling a function is found when that function returns one: `createIconLoader("lucide")`, whose function returns a rendering function with typed props, and `generateCalendar<Dayjs>(config)`, whose generic arrow returns a local asserted to a component type. On shadcn/ui that adds `IconLucide` and four more icon loaders; on Ant Design, `Calendar`. A call to a function that returns anything else is left out, and no longer produces a skipped-candidate note (9 fewer on Ant Design, 18 on shadcn/ui). The new `factoryResult` detection rule appears in `detectedBy`.
crates/binding/CHANGELOG.md:42:- Components built with `createElement` or `forwardRef` in a plain `.ts` file are now found when the file imports a value from React, where they were never looked for before. Files with no React import are still skipped. No action needed.
crates/binding/CHANGELOG.md:56:- Components are now found by the shape of the code instead of the names it uses: `memo(forwardRef(function Button(props: ButtonProps, ref) {…}))` with no type arguments is a component with a `ref`, React's `forwardRef`, `memo` and `createContext` are recognized under any import alias or namespace, and a tagged factory such as `chakra("div", {…})` takes the props type declared beside it that gives its tag (`interface CenterProps extends HTMLChakraProps<"div">`) rather than whichever type is named `{Name}Props`. A props type another component already takes is never reused, and a tag-only factory whose file declares no matching props type is skipped with a diagnostic.
crates/binding/CHANGELOG.md:147:  - **Session start no longer serializes every prop:** the new `initializeSessionIndex` returns only each component's file, name and the diagnostics. Chakra with dependencies skips a 25 MB JSON round trip.
crates/binding/CHANGELOG.md:168:  - **Fewer skip diagnostics:** a PascalCase local that matches no component pattern (`const Comp = asChild ? Slot : "button"`) is no longer reported.
crates/binding/CHANGELOG.md:189:- - **Functions used only as functions are no longer reported as components:** a PascalCase function that returns JSX but is only ever called in its file (`ArrayType(type)`), or that takes a second parameter such as a ref and is never rendered or passed to a component wrapper (a render callback like `{render: TableDropIndicatorWrapper}`), is now a skipped candidate with the reason. Exported functions are unaffected. On React Spectrum this removes 25 false components.

# Pinned to callisto 0.20.0 in .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml.
# Callisto checks build attestations against that exact workflow filename; do not rename it.

# `match` is a package name ("<ecosystem>/<name>"), never a directory path.
# Root package.json is `caliper-docgen-workspace` so bare `caliper-docgen` stays unambiguous.

[changesets]
dir = ".changeset"

[cascade]
mode = "out-of-range"
bump-severity = "patch"
peer-escalation = true
preserve-npm-ranges = true

# The CLI binaries ship as assets of the one GitHub Release for the product package.
# The npm `bin` of `npm/caliper-docgen` cannot be a product, so the product is the Cargo crate.
# `target` matches the build matrix in callisto-release.yml; `asset-name` is the exact file name.
[release]
product-package = "cargo/caliper-docgen"
forge-repository = "orin-dx/caliper"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/caliper-docgen"
target = "aarch64-apple-darwin"
asset-name = "caliper-docgen-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/caliper-docgen"
target = "x86_64-apple-darwin"
asset-name = "caliper-docgen-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/caliper-docgen"
target = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
asset-name = "caliper-docgen-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/caliper-docgen"
target = "aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu"

== .changeset/supervisor-does-not-restart.md
---
cargo/caliper-docgen-tsc-client: minor
---

The `tsc` supervisor no longer restarts a crashed process, because nothing used it to; `caliper-docgen-semantic` runs its own restart policy. `Supervisor::request` is gone (send requests through `Supervisor::client()`, which was already the way to do it), as are the error variant `TscClientError::RestartStormDetected` and the supervisor's restart cap and backoff. A session that ends stays ended, and `Supervisor::is_alive` is false from then on; spawn a new `Supervisor` to start again.
== .changeset/tsc-client-raw-answers.md
---
cargo/caliper-docgen-tsc-client: minor
---

For library users: `Client::request_raw` answers with a `RawResponse`, the response's `result` as the JSON text it arrived as, so a caller that knows the shape it expects parses it once, straight into that shape, instead of first into a `serde_json::Value`. `Client::request` answers as before. Frames are now read in one pass, which makes every answer cheaper to receive; caliper's checker backend uses the raw form, and on Chakra's `Button` (852 props) its first answer is about 25% faster.
== .changeset/on-demand-reports-recycles.md
---
cargo/caliper-docgen-semantic: minor
---

For library users: `OnDemand::recycles()` reports how many times the warm checker's process was replaced on purpose, split into `worn` (it built its 64 programs) and `bloated` (it passed `max_rss_mib`), and `OnDemand::process_id()` names the process that answered last. Replacements are also logged at debug level. Nothing changes for the CLI, the addon or the output.

crates/cli/CHANGELOG.md:12:- The experimental TypeScript checker can now run on `tsrs` (`npm i tsrs`) as well as on `typescript@beta`. Caliper finds `node_modules/tsrs/bin/tsrs` when no `typescript` 7.1 is installed, and `--tsc-path` (or `tscPath`) also takes the `@tsrs/<platform>/tsrs` binary, which used to fail with "could not determine tsc's version". content.content:
---
cargo/caliper-docgen-core: minor
---

The unused plugin system is removed from `caliper-docgen-core`: `DocgenPlugin`, `PluginRegistry`, the `plugin` module and the `plugins` field of `PipelineOptions` no longer exist. Nothing in the CLI, the Vite plugin or the Storybook addon could register a plugin, so extraction output is unchanged. Code that implemented `DocgenPlugin` or set `PipelineOptions.plugins` needs to drop it.
---
cargo/caliper-docgen-core: minor
cargo/caliper-docgen-semantic: patch
cargo/caliper-docgen: minor
cargo/caliper-docgen-napi: minor
npm/caliper-docgen: minor
npm/caliper-docgen-napi: minor
npm/caliper-docgen-storybook: minor
npm/caliper-docgen-vite-plugin: patch
---

The built-in TypeScript checker now answers by default (ADR 0026). `extract`, `check` and `inspect` merge its answer over the structural one, prop by prop, and wait for it. A native session and the Storybook addon ask it for each component a request names, and still show the structural props first when it is slower than `semanticWaitMs` (150 ms). `--no-checker`, or `checker: false` in `docgen.config.ts`, the native options or the addon's options, runs the structural resolver alone, as before. `watch`, `extractAll` and the Vite plugin stay structural.

The checker costs time and memory. `extract` of an app with 938 Chakra UI and MUI components takes about 6 s and 970 MiB, against 0.1 s and 200 MiB with `--no-checker`. A session that answered every one of them peaks at about 1 GB, against 380 MiB without the checker: each answer the session keeps now shares its props with the others, where before each kept its own copy, about 6.7 MiB per Chakra component.

Breaking: `--experimental-semantic-types`, the config's `experimentalSemanticTypes` and the `semanticTypes` option of the native binding and the Storybook addon are removed. The CLI and the config reject the old names as unknown, and the addon rejects `semanticTypes` by name. `PipelineOptions::experimental_semantic_types` is now `PipelineOptions::checker`, and it is `true` by default.

Action: drop `--experimental-semantic-types`, `experimentalSemanticTypes: true` and `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'`, since the checker now runs without them. Replace `semanticTypes: 'off'`, or a run that relied on the old structural default, with `checker: false` or `--no-checker`.
---
cargo/caliper-docgen-semantic: patch
cargo/caliper-docgen-core: patch
cargo/caliper-docgen: patch
npm/caliper-docgen: patch
---

A whole-project `extract` with the checker (the default) is about three to four times as fast, with the same output. On an app wrapping the 938 components of Chakra UI and MUI it takes 1.8 s instead of 6.2 s, and 1.4 s instead of 5.7 s for the 787 Chakra components alone; `react-docgen-typescript` takes 7.3 s and 4.1 s on the same files. The checker's answer for a prop that many components share (Chakra's style props) is now converted and merged once instead of once per component, the answers are read on several threads, and the built-in checker answers two programs over the same files at once. Peak memory is about 10% higher (1.1 GiB instead of 0.98 on that app; 1.5 GiB on three copies of it). The Storybook session and a checker run through `--tsc-path` keep asking one program.

Without the build step the suite skips, which is green but covers nothing; a job that must run it should check that the binary exists first.

## tsrs parity

ADR 0026 makes the Go checker (`typescript-beta`) the type authority and lets tsrs, the Rust port, stand in for it only while it agrees. `construct:parity` is that agreement check: it runs the same one-program capture as `construct:capture` once with the Go checker and once with the exact `tsrs` version pinned in `apps/oracle/package.json`, normalizes both through `src/oracle-checker.ts`, and compares every row on four facts: the normalized type, the `typeToString` text, and the prop type's `flags` and `intrinsicName` (the facts Caliper reads through the API to tell the error type from `any`). It needs no corpora and no network, and takes a couple of seconds.

```sh
pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:parity   # or: just test-parity
```

Run it on every tsrs bump, before changing the pin in the version allow-lists (`crates/tsc-client/src/supervisor.rs`, `crates/semantic/src/lib.rs`), together with the construct suite. Bump the `tsrs` devDependency of `apps/oracle` first, run it, and change the Rust pins only when it passes. The weekly oracle keeps the Go checker as the independent arbiter; this run does not replace it.

A reported difference is a row where tsrs gives a different answer than the Go checker. The report names the row, both `typeToString` texts, the differing facts, and a diff of the two normalized forms (`-` Go, `+` tsrs). Treat it as a tsrs bug or a protocol change until shown otherwise: do not pin that tsrs version, and report it upstream.

`parity-allowlist.json` maps a row id to the reason its difference is harmless (for example a lib file path inside an `import("...")` text). Add an entry only for a difference that cannot change the type Caliper reports, and give the reason. An entry whose row stops differing, or names no row, fails the run, so the list stays honest: remove it. The list is empty while every row is identical.

`tests/construct-parity.test.ts` runs the same comparison in-process. It skips with a warning when `tsrs` is not installed; set `REQUIRE_TSRS=1` to fail instead.

## The checker lane

ADR 0026's gate before the default flipped, kept as the checker path's: the suite through the checker (the default since S8, here with the pinned `tsrs` through `--tsc-path`, and `--no-resolver-facts`, so a default and a union's member order come from the checker and oxc's syntax, not the structural resolver), held to `checker-expectations.json`, which has the shape of `expectations.json`. Green rows must stay green; every other row is a documented gap with a one-line reason. The lane fails when a row is better or worse than its entry (an improvement means the gap closed: update the entry and drop the `gap`), when the checker did not answer for a row, or when the backend was unavailable.

```sh
just test-checker-lane   # CI job "Test / Checker lane"
```

The recipe builds the release binary, then runs `construct:check`, `construct:parity`, the lane (`construct:checker`) and `tests/construct-checker-lane.test.ts` with `REQUIRE_TSRS=1 REQUIRE_CALIPER_BIN=1`, so a missing binary fails instead of skipping. `TSRS_BIN` is the native binary the `tsrs` package itself selects (`src/tsrs-bin.ts` calls its `lib/getExePath.js`): `node_modules/@tsrs/<os>-<arch>[-gnu|-musl]/tsrs`. The `bin/tsrs` shim is a Node launcher and is not used. Regenerate an entry by running `CALIPER_SEMANTIC=1 TSRS_BIN=<path> pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:checker` and reading the report.

ADR 0026's S4 gate is that the checker path equals the structural path except listed improvements. The lane and `tests/construct-checker-lane.test.ts` (which needs no binary, so it runs with the package tests) hold the two files to it: a row whose checker verdicts rank below its `expectations.json` verdicts fails unless its `checker-expectations.json` entry gives an `"improvement"` reason, the case where the comparison scores the checker's answer lower although it states more (no row needs one today: `react/34` did until the comparator read `Omit<HTMLAttributes<…>>` as one family). An `"improvement"` on a row that does not rank below the structural path fails too, so the list stays honest. Rows the checker ranks above the structural path are improvements already explained by the structural `gap`. A member keyed by a symbol (`[tag]`) is read by `src/caliper-norm.ts` as the checker side states it.

## Not covered

Constructs the fixture format (one self-contained file, one prop `p`, no runtime code) cannot express, or that were left out:

- `declare const enum`: ambient const enums error under `isolatedModules` (TS2748); a local `const enum` is `literals/19`.
- Computed enum members (`E.A = 1 << 2`): left out to stay on common spellings.

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen
    export REQUIRE_TSRS=1 REQUIRE_CALIPER_BIN=1 CALIPER_BIN="$PWD/target/release/caliper-docgen"
    TSRS_BIN="$(pnpm --silent --filter caliper-docgen-oracle exec tsx src/tsrs-bin.ts)"
    export TSRS_BIN
    echo "tsrs: $TSRS_BIN"
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:check""", """# The checker gates of ADR 0026, with nothing allowed to skip: the golden check, tsrs-against-Go parity, and the construct

content.content:
1	# Semantic backend (TypeScript 7)
2	
3	**Status:** the checker is the default ([ADR 0026](adr/0026-the-checker-is-the-type-authority.md) S8, see "The checker is the default" below): `extract`, `check`, `inspect`, napi sessions and the Storybook addon ask it, and `--no-checker` (`checker: false`) turns it off. It began as an opt-in second resolver ([ADR 0006](adr/0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md), [ADR 0007](adr/0007-backend-discovers-components-and-compiles-in.md), "Slice 1" below); its answer wins prop by prop (see "The checker's answer wins"). The checker is built in (the `tsrs` crates, see "The checker"); `--tsc-path` runs a binary instead. Structural extraction is the fallback, and what `--no-checker`, `watch` and the Vite plugin run. Separately, TypeScript 7.1's checker runs as a test-only oracle for structural prop types (`scripts/weekly.py --oracle`, `docs/measurement.md`). **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 for slice 1 against `7.1.0-beta`; 2026-09-27 for the Cost measurements, each naming its nightly; 2026-10-22 for the API table against the `7.1.0-beta` package; 2026-10-23 for the fixture-corpus parity on `7.1.0-beta`.
4	
5	## Next step
6	
7	Slice 1 below covers function components by their export. Next, in order: set what `PropType` now carries (index signatures, `readonly`, a ref type's name; optional and rest parameters are done; per-prop `tags` and `parent` are done, see S7a below), class components (generic ones are read at their default: "Generic components" below), and `batchRequests` to cut round trips; watch-mode notifications are done ("Watch" below). The NAPI binding already ships: a session asks a warm checker for the requested component (on by default, ADR 0022). The client's open Lifecycle items in the Gates table still stand.
8	
9	Some props can't be resolved from the AST alone. The checker backend asks TypeScript's checker instead, using the algorithm react-docgen-typescript (RDT) uses, and merges the answer into the structural result. It runs by default (ADR 0026 S8).
10	
11	## What the structural resolver can't do
12	
13	Component prop counts from `fixtures/` with `--html-attributes full`, against RDT. Root causes are from `docs/benchmarks.md`.
14	
15	| Gap | Example | Ours | RDT |
16	| --- | --- | --: | --: |
17	| Generics through alias chains | ariakit `Props<T, O> = O & Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<T>, keyof O>` | 5 | 294 |
18	| Generics through alias chains | ark-ui `SelectRoot` | 36 | 314 |
19	| Conditional types | headlessui `PropsOf<TTag>` | 14 | 246 |
20	| Mapped types over a generic | base-ui `WithBaseUIEvent<T>` | 11 | 293 |
21	| Conditional type and indexed access | fluentui `Slot<Type, ...>` | 8 | 303 |
22	| `@emotion/styled` two-argument overload | storybook-emotion `Button` | 7 | 306 |
23	
24	In the 2026-07-25 baseline, 10 of 33 compared components account for 2,696 of 2,720 missing props. The other 24 are `ref` and `key`, which this tool omits by design (`MIGRATING.md`).
25	
26	## How it works
27	
28	```
29	OXC parse → structural resolver ─────────────────┐
30	                                                 ├→ merge → ExtractionOutput
31	tsrs (built in) → semantic resolver (default) ──┘
32	```
33	
34	The structural result is complete on its own and returns first. The semantic pass reads each exported component from the checker and replaces the structural props where it finds one.
35	
36	### Merge rules (proposed)
37	
38	| Field | Source |
39	| --- | --- |
40	| Props present, `type`, `required` | Semantic. A `type` the checker could not read (an `opaque` part) where the structural one is read in full stays structural, marked (see "The checker's answer wins") |
41	| `parent`, `declarations` | Semantic. `declarations` lists every declaring interface, not just the first |
42	| `description`, `tags` | Semantic JSDoc, structural if empty |
43	| `composes` | Semantic: the `@types/react` types the props type is made of |
44	| `defaultValue` | oxc: the component's code (a destructured parameter's initializer, `defaultProps`), else the checker's `@default` tag; structural where neither has one (S7a2) |
45	| Components tsc doesn't surface (not exported) | Structural only |
46	| Structural diagnostics of a resolved component | Dropped where the checker's answer supersedes them (see "Diagnostics a checker answer supersedes") |
47	
48	### What gets dropped, and where
49	
50	| Dropped | Where | Status |
51	| --- | --- | --- |
52	| `children` without a description | RDT projection only. Canonical keeps it | Done |
53	| Ambient `.d.ts` components such as `PureComponent` | Merge step | Done |
54	| `key` | Not emitted, matching the structural path | Closed |
55	| `ref` | Emitted in `curated` and `full` for `ComponentProps<"div">`-style props and `forwardRef` components, matching the structural path | Closed |
56	| HTML and DOM attributes in curated and none mode | Semantic adapter, by declaring interface rather than by name | Open |
57	
58	### Delivery (proposed)
59	
60	The structural result returns immediately. The semantic result follows: the CLI waits for it, and the NAPI binding exposes a second async call so the Vite plugin can patch when it resolves. Spawn `tsc` at the start of the run so it loads while extraction runs. Each result carries a content hash, and a stale one is dropped.
61	
62	## Slice 1 (the first opt-in, now the default)
63	
64	`caliper-docgen extract [--tsc-path PATH]`, or `tscPath` in `docgen.config.ts` (it was `--experimental-semantic-types` until S8; `--no-checker`, or `checker: false` in the config, turns it off). `crates/semantic` asks the checker built into caliper, or with `--tsc-path` a checker binary it runs as `--api` process (see "The checker"), builds one program over the files of the components the structural pass found, and asks for each exported function component its call signature's first parameter and that type's properties. The CLI then calls core's `merge_semantic`. Since S8 `check` asks it too, and `inspect` for the one component it shows; `watch` does not, and the NAPI binding asks per component (below).
65	
66	- **Merge:** props present, `type`, `required`, `parent`, `declarations` and the component's `composes` from the checker, and its description and tags where it has them (see "Declarations, tags and composes"); `defaultValue`, inheritance layers, curated inherited props and `discriminantProp` stay structural. The checker is asked for a prop's description only when the structural pass has none (65% of Mantine's requests otherwise). Props `@types/react` declares are excluded by declaring file. Identical merged props are shared, as in the structural result.
67	- **Output type:** no new `PropType` variant and no schema change. Primitives, literals, unions (with `boolean` collapsed and `undefined` dropped from optional props), arrays, tuples, inline objects of up to 16 fields and single-signature functions map onto existing variants; `ReactNode`, `ElementType`, `CSSProperties` and `ReactElement` map to their terminals; anything else (named interfaces, enums, generics, overloads, anything past depth 4) is `Named` with the checker's own text. Union members keep the checker's order, which is creation order, not source order.
68	- **Names:** a symbol's `name` from the checker is its escaped name: a name that starts with two underscores has a third (`__size` arrives as `___size`, TypeScript's `escapeLeadingUnderscores`, so that it cannot collide with internal names such as `__call`). `rpc.rs` removes it when the answer is read, so every name downstream is the one the source writes.
69	- **Error type:** a name the checker cannot resolve (an import that does not resolve, a name declared nowhere) is typed with its error type, which carries the flags of `any`. Only `Type.intrinsicName` tells it from a written `any`: `"error"` against `"any"`, and the error type has an id per site, so the `any` id says nothing. `rpc.rs` reads `intrinsicName`; `convert.rs` turns an `"error"` type into an `opaque` type with the reason `unresolvableImport` (its `specifier` is the name as the source writes it, since the checker does not say which module was behind it), so the prop has `degradedBy: ["unresolvableImport"]` and a written `any` stays `any` with none. No new diagnostic code.
70	- **Provenance:** `Info` diagnostics with code `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` whose `affects` lists the output keys: one for the components the checker resolved, one per fallback reason. A first-class per-component field would change the canonical JSON and needs a `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump (`crates/core/src/types/output.rs`).
71	- **Fallback:** a missing, unsupported-version, crashed or timed-out `tsc` gives the structural result plus one `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` warning, never an error. Per component, the structural result stands for: not exported, class or non-function, overloaded, no props parameter, `any`/`unknown`/union props type, a generic component whose instantiation at its default could not be formed (see "Generic components"), none of the exports the extractor recorded for it found (or found declared in another file), a generic sub-component reached through its parent's property, or a request the checker rejected. Each is listed with its reason.
72	- **Which export:** the extractor records how the module exports each component (ADR 0027): its export names (`default` included), or for a sub-component attached to an exported one the path through that export (`Menu.Item = Item` beside `export default Menu` is `default.Item`). The checker asks for exactly those, follows an alias to what it aliases, reads an attached sub-component as the property of its parent's type, and checks that the declaration is in the component's file. It never takes the module's `default` unless `default` is a recorded export, and never looks a component up by its display name. Each request carries the component's output key, its answer or fallback carries it back, and the merge (whole-project and session, in time or late) finds the entry by that key alone.
73	- **Parameter markers:** the checker's parameter symbols carry no optional or rest flag (an optional parameter has the same flags and `checkFlags` as a required one), so `convert.rs` reads them from what the checker prints for the function type: `name?: T` is optional and its `undefined` is dropped from the type, as for an optional prop, `...name: T[]` is the rest parameter; the signature's `flags` (`HasRestParameter`, bit 1) say the last parameter is a rest parameter either way. A parameter whose type is written `T | undefined` stays required. The type is printed with `typeToString` flags `NoTruncation | InTypeAlias` (plus the checker's own defaults): an alias at the top (`type Handler = (value?: string) => void`) is printed as the parameter list it stands for, not as `Handler`, and nothing is cut short. A `this` parameter is printed but is not one of the signature's parameters, and an overload set or a function with properties is printed as an object type whose signatures are read in order. When the printed type still does not give one entry per parameter (a callable interface prints as its name whatever the flags), a parameter is never taken to be required: the type is `opaque` with reason `unsupportedExpression`, so the prop carries `degradedBy`.
74	- **Not carried:** index signatures, `readonly` and ref names (`PropType` has them since `SCHEMA_VERSION` 4; `convert.rs` doesn't set them), generic parameters of functions.
75	- **Tests:** `crates/semantic/tests/replay.rs` runs the backend against `replay-tsc`, which answers from a recording of the real `7.1.0-beta` (`tests/fixtures/recording.json`, refreshed by `cargo run -p caliper-docgen-semantic --example record_fixture -- <typescript package dir>`; the `markers` fixture project, for names and parameters, records to `tests/fixtures/markers.recording.json` with the fixture name as a second argument; the `errors` fixture records the error type); a request the recording lacks fails the test. Fallbacks (no `tsc`, unsupported version, bad path, crash, hang) are asserted as the structural output plus one warning. The CLI test asserts the default output has no `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` diagnostic.
76	
77	Measured on `7.1.0-beta`, `extract --json` (best of 2 to 3), flag on against off, plus the base commit's output compared byte for byte (identical apart from `durationMs` on all five corpora, with and without `--load-dependencies`). Peak RSS is the larger of the two processes; on Chakra Caliper is 117 MiB and `tsc` 945 MiB.
78	
79	| Corpus   | Components resolved by the checker |            Off |              On |
80	| -------- | ---------------------------------: | -------------: | --------------: |
81	| mantine  |                          332 / 344 |  47 ms, 82 MiB | 588 ms, 287 MiB |
82	| chakra   |                          598 / 598 |  38 ms, 68 MiB |  9.3 s, 975 MiB |
83	| shadcn   |                      1,693 / 1,884 |  48 ms, 81 MiB |  1.5 s, 874 MiB |
84	| antd     |                          206 / 248 |  36 ms, 69 MiB | 508 ms, 443 MiB |
85	| spectrum |                      1,153 / 1,356 | 71 ms, 118 MiB | 618 ms, 381 MiB |
86	
87	Chakra's time is `tsc` computing 470,000 shared props' types, not round trips. Before shared props were interned in the merge, Caliper itself held 7.4 GiB on Chakra.
88	
89	Against the oracle (`scripts/weekly.py --oracle`, flag on, `7.1.0-beta`), wrong verdicts fall to 0.0% on every corpus but antd (0.1%), but the identical-or-spelled share also falls: mantine 91.3% to 22.0%, chakra 100% to 16.4%, shadcn 85.2% to 52.3%, antd 91.9% to 82.3%, spectrum 83.2% to 28.3%. The oracle credits the structural result for keeping a type's name (`StyleProp<MantineSpacing>`); the checker's answer is expanded to its members and compared as "less precise". Keeping the alias name and arguments needs a `PropType` that carries them, which is an output change.
90	
91	### The checker
92	
93	The checker is built in: the `tsrs` crates (`tsrs_api`, `tsrs_vfs`, pinned `=0.24.0`, TypeScript `3e9236361fa9`, the commit of `typescript@7.1.0-beta`) linked into the CLI and the napi binding. Nothing is installed and no project `typescript` is looked for. It runs by default since S8.
94	
95	- **Its own threads.** `crates/semantic/src/checker.rs` creates a `tsrs_api::Session` on a thread of its own with a 512 MiB stack, the stack the `tsrs` binary serves on: a query runs on the calling thread, and a type 2,000 deep overflows a default 2 MiB thread, which aborts the process. Requests from any thread reach it over a channel and are answered one at a time; a whole-project `extract` starts a second thread with a channel (a lane) of its own and asks a snapshot of two programs over the same root files, each program's requests down its own lane (`tsrs_api` locks a program's one checker for the length of a request, so two programs are what can be answered at once). Every program holds every root file, so either answers a component as one program would; the Storybook session and a checker process ask one; `Session::handle_request` is the dispatcher the `tsrs` binary serves, so `rpc.rs` sends the same methods and JSON over either route. A panic inside the checker comes back as an error for that request (`tsrs_api` catches it) and the session keeps answering; a stack overflow still aborts (deep-type tests: 2,000 levels in every run, 10,000 in release).
96	- **Lib files.** The crates embed TypeScript's lib, so a lib declaration's file is `bundled:///libs/lib.dom.d.ts` where a process names the file in its install. The path classifiers read the file name (`lib.*.d.ts`), so both are the lib (`tests/tsrs_real.rs`).
97	- **Same diagnostics.** A checker thread that cannot start, a request past its deadline and a stopped checker give the `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` warning the process route gives.
98	
99	`--tsc-path` (or `tscPath`) runs a checker binary as an `--api` process instead, through `crates/tsc-client`, and must exist; this is how the Go `typescript` beta runs as the oracle and the parity gate (`CALIPER_TEST_TSC` in the tests, `TSRS_BIN` in the checker lane). Two packages provide one:
100	
101	- **`typescript`** from 7.1 on (`7.1.0-beta`, rc and stable): `node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc`.
102	- **`tsrs`** (`oxc-project/tsrs`): `node_modules/tsrs/bin/tsrs`, a Node shim that starts the platform binary from `@tsrs/<platform>`, which can be given directly too. Traced on the wire against `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`: the same method sequence and the same results as `typescript@7.1.0-beta` on three recordings.
103	
104	**Version rule** (`crates/tsc-client/src/supervisor.rs`, list in `crates/semantic/src/lib.rs`, `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS`). The version is read from the `package.json` of the package that owns the binary: the parent of `bin` for `typescript/bin/tsc` and `tsrs/bin/tsrs`, the binary's own directory for `@tsrs/<platform>/tsrs`. An entry is an exact version or a `major.minor` series. A `tsrs` version reads `<tsrs version>-ts<typescript version>`; it is accepted only when it is listed exactly (today `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, the build that was traced) and its TypeScript part is also taken by a TypeScript entry (`7.1`). A new `tsrs` release is therefore refused until someone traces it and adds it, as for any other build.
105	
106	The protocol detail that matters for `tsrs` is unchanged from `typescript`: the client sends `createPrograms[].compilerOptions` (the Node client sends `options`; the server accepts both, and `crates/semantic/tests/replay.rs` pins the key). # Semantic backend (TypeScript 7)

**Status:** the checker is the default ([ADR 0026](adr/0026-the-checker-is-the-type-authority.md) S8, see "The checker is the default" below): `extract`, `check`, `inspect`, napi sessions and the Storybook addon ask it, and `--no-checker` (`checker: false`) turns it off. It began as an opt-in second resolver ([ADR 0006](adr/0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md), [ADR 0007](adr/0007-backend-discovers-components-and-compiles-in.md), "Slice 1" below); its answer wins prop by prop (see "The checker's answer wins"). The checker is built in (the `tsrs` crates, see "The checker"); `--tsc-path` runs a binary instead. Structural extraction is the fallback, and what `--no-checker`, `watch` and the Vite plugin run. Separately, TypeScript 7.1's checker runs as a test-only oracle for structural prop types (`scripts/weekly.py --oracle`, `docs/measurement.md`). **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 for slice 1 against `7.1.0-beta`; 2026-09-27 for the Cost measurements, each naming its nightly; 2026-10-22 for the API table against the `7.1.0-beta` package; 2026-10-23 for the fixture-corpus parity on `7.1.0-beta`.

## Next step

Slice 1 below covers function components by their export. Next, in order: set what `PropType` now carries (index signatures, `readonly`, a ref type's name; optional and rest parameters are done; per-prop `tags` and `parent` are done, see S7a below), class components (generic ones are read at their default: "Generic components" below), and `batchRequests` to cut round trips; watch-mode notifications are done ("Watch" below). The NAPI binding already ships: a session asks a warm checker for the requested component (on by default, ADR 0022). The client's open Lifecycle items in the Gates table still stand.

Some props can't be resolved from the AST alone. The checker backend asks TypeScript's checker instead, using the algorithm react-docgen-typescript (RDT) uses, and merges the answer into the structural result. It runs by default (ADR 0026 S8).

## What the structural resolver can't do

Component prop counts from `fixtures/` with `--html-attributes full`, against RDT. Root causes are from `docs/benchmarks.md`.

| Gap | Example | Ours | RDT |
| --- | --- | --: | --: |
| Generics through alias chains | ariakit `Props<T, O> = O & Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<T>, keyof O>` | 5 | 294 |
| Generics through alias chains | ark-ui `SelectRoot` | 36 | 314 |
| Conditional types | headlessui `PropsOf<TTag>` | 14 | 246 |
| Mapped types over a generic | base-ui `WithBaseUIEvent<T>` | 11 | 293 |
| Conditional type and indexed access | fluentui `Slot<Type, ...>` | 8 | 303 |
| `@emotion/styled` two-argument overload | storybook-emotion `Button` | 7 | 306 |

In the 2026-07-25 baseline, 10 of 33 compared components account for 2,696 of 2,720 missing props. The other 24 are `ref` and `key`, which this tool omits by design (`MIGRATING.md`).

## How it works

```
OXC parse → structural resolver ─────────────────┐
                                                 ├→ merge → ExtractionOutput
tsrs (built in) → semantic resolver (default) ──┘
```

The structural result is complete on its own and returns first. The semantic pass reads each exported component from the checker and replaces the structural props where it finds one.

### Merge rules (proposed)

| Field | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Props present, `type`, `required` | Semantic. A `type` the checker could not read (an `opaque` part) where the structural one is read in full stays structural, marked (see "The checker's answer wins") |
| `parent`, `declarations` | Semantic. `declarations` lists every declaring interface, not just the first |
| `description`, `tags` | Semantic JSDoc, structural if empty |
| `composes` | Semantic: the `@types/react` types the props type is made of |
| `defaultValue` | oxc: the component's code (a destructured parameter's initializer, `defaultProps`), else the checker's `@default` tag; structural where neither has one (S7a2) |
| Components tsc doesn't surface (not exported) | Structural only |
| Structural diagnostics of a resolved component | Dropped where the checker's answer supersedes them (see "Diagnostics a checker answer supersedes") |

### What gets dropped, and where

| Dropped | Where | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` without a description | RDT projection only. Canonical keeps it | Done |
| Ambient `.d.ts` components such as `PureComponent` | Merge step | Done |
| `key` | Not emitted, matching the structural path | Closed |
| `ref` | Emitted in `curated` and `full` for `ComponentProps<"div">`-style props and `forwardRef` components, matching the structural path | Closed |
| HTML and DOM attributes in curated and none mode | Semantic adapter, by declaring interface rather than by name | Open |

### Delivery (proposed)

The structural result returns immediately. The semantic result follows: the CLI waits for it, and the NAPI binding exposes a second async call so the Vite plugin can patch when it resolves. Spawn `tsc` at the start of the run so it loads while extraction runs. Each result carries a content hash, and a stale one is dropped.

## Slice 1 (the first opt-in, now the default)

`caliper-docgen extract [--tsc-path PATH]`, or `tscPath` in `docgen.config.ts` (it was `--experimental-semantic-types` until S8; `--no-checker`, or `checker: false` in the config, turns it off). `crates/semantic` asks the checker built into caliper, or with `--tsc-path` a checker binary it runs as `--api` process (see "The checker"), builds one program over the files of the components the structural pass found, and asks for each exported function component its call signature's first parameter and that type's properties. The CLI then calls core's `merge_semantic`. Since S8 `check` asks it too, and `inspect` for the one component it shows; `watch` does not, and the NAPI binding asks per component (below).

- **Merge:** props present, `type`, `required`, `parent`, `declarations` and the component's `composes` from the checker, and its description and tags where it has them (see "Declarations, tags and composes"); `defaultValue`, inheritance layers, curated inherited props and `discriminantProp` stay structural. The checker is asked for a prop's description only when the structural pass has none (65% of Mantine's requests otherwise). Props `@types/react` declares are excluded by declaring file. Identical merged props are shared, as in the structural result.
- **Output type:** no new `PropType` variant and no schema change. Primitives, literals, unions (with `boolean` collapsed and `undefined` dropped from optional props), arrays, tuples, inline objects of up to 16 fields and single-signature functions map onto existing variants; `ReactNode`, `ElementType`, `CSSProperties` and `ReactElement` map to their terminals; anything else (named interfaces, enums, generics, overloads, anything past depth 4) is `Named` with the checker's own text. Union members keep the checker's order, which is creation order, not source order.
- **Names:** a symbol's `name` from the checker is its escaped name: a name that starts with two underscores has a third (`__size` arrives as `___size`, TypeScript's `escapeLeadingUnderscores`, so that it cannot collide with internal names such as `__call`). `rpc.rs` removes it when the answer is read, so every name downstream is the one the source writes.
- **Error type:** a name the checker cannot resolve (an import that does not resolve, a name declared nowhere) is typed with its error type, which carries the flags of `any`. No new diagnostic code.
- **Provenance:** `Info` diagnostics with code `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` whose `affects` lists the output keys: one for the components the checker resolved, one per fallback reason. A first-class per-component field would change the canonical JSON and needs a `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump (`crates/core/src/types/output.rs`).
- **Fallback:** a missing, unsupported-version, crashed or timed-out `tsc` gives the structural result plus one `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` warning, never an error. Per component, the structural result stands for: not exported, class or non-function, overloaded, no props parameter, `any`/`unknown`/union props type, a generic component whose instantiation at its default could not be formed (see "Generic components"), none of the exports the extractor recorded for it found (or found declared in another file), a generic sub-component reached through its parent's property, or a request the checker rejected. Each is listed with its reason.
- **Which export:** the extractor records how the module exports each component (ADR 0027): its export names (`default` included), or for a sub-component attached to an exported one the path through that export (`Menu.Item = Item` beside `export default Menu` is `default.Item`). The checker asks for exactly those, follows an alias to what it aliases, reads an attached sub-component as the property of its parent's type, and checks that the declaration is in the component's file. It never takes the module's `default` unless `default` is a recorded export, and never looks a component up by its display name. Each request carries the component's output key, its answer or fallback carries it back, and the merge (whole-project and session, in time or late) finds the entry by that key alone.
- **Parameter markers:** the checker's parameter symbols carry no optional or rest flag (an optional parameter has the same flags and `checkFlags` as a required one), so `convert.rs` reads them from what the checker prints for the function type: `name?: T` is optional and its `undefined` is dropped from the type, as for an optional prop, `...name: T[]` is the rest parameter; the signature's `flags` (`HasRestParameter`, bit 1) say the last parameter is a rest parameter either way. A parameter whose type is written `T | undefined` stays required. The type is printed with `typeToString` flags `NoTruncation | InTypeAlias` (plus the checker's own defaults): an alias at the top (`type Handler = (value?: string) => void`) is printed as the parameter list it stands for, not as `Handler`, and nothing is cut short. A `this` parameter is printed but is not one of the signature's parameters, and an overload set or a function with properties is printed as an object type whose signatures are read in order. When the printed type still does not give one entry per parameter (a callable interface prints as its name whatever the flags), a parameter is never taken to be required: the type is `opaque` with reason `unsupportedExpression`, so the prop carries `degradedBy`.
- **Not carried:** index signatures, `readonly` and ref names (`PropType` has them since `SCHEMA_VERSION` 4; `convert.rs` doesn't set them), generic parameters of functions.
- **Tests:** `crates/semantic/tests/replay.rs` runs the backend against `replay-tsc`, which answers from a recording of the real `7.1.0-beta` (`tests/fixtures/recording.json`, refreshed by `cargo run -p caliper-docgen-semantic --example record_fixture -- <typescript package dir>`; the `markers` fixture project, for names and parameters, records to `tests/fixtures/markers.recording.json` with the fixture name as a second argument; the `errors` fixture records the error type); a request the recording lacks fails the test. Fallbacks (no `tsc`, unsupported version, bad path, crash, hang) are asserted as the structural output plus one warning. The CLI test asserts the default output has no `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` diagnostic.

Measured on `7.1.0-beta`, `extract --json` (best of 2 to 3), flag on against off, plus the base commit's output compared byte for byte (identical apart from `durationMs` on all five corpora, with and without `--load-dependencies`). Peak RSS is the larger of the two processes; on Chakra Caliper is 117 MiB and `tsc` 945 MiB.

| Corpus   | Components resolved by the checker |            Off |              On |
| -------- | ---------------------------------: | -------------: | --------------: |
| mantine  |                          332 / 344 |  47 ms, 82 MiB | 588 ms, 287 MiB |
| chakra   |                          598 / 598 |  38 ms, 68 MiB |  9.3 s, 975 MiB |
| shadcn   |                      1,693 / 1,884 |  48 ms, 81 MiB |  1.5 s, 874 MiB |
| antd     |                          206 / 248 |  36 ms, 69 MiB | 508 ms, 443 MiB |
| spectrum |                      1,153 / 1,356 | 71 ms, 118 MiB | 618 ms, 381 MiB |

Chakra's time is `tsc` computing 470,000 shared props' types, not round trips. Before shared props were interned in the merge, Caliper itself held 7.4 GiB on Chakra.

Against the oracle (`scripts/weekly.py --oracle`, flag on, `7.1.0-beta`), wrong verdicts fall to 0.0% on every corpus but antd (0.1%), but the identical-or-spelled share also falls: mantine 91.3% to 22.0%, chakra 100% to 16.4%, shadcn 85.2% to 52.3%, antd 91.9% to 82.3%, spectrum 83.2% to 28.3%.
