rep("""The checker is built in (the `tsrs` crates, see "The checker"); `--tsc-path` runs a binary instead. Structural extraction""",
    """The checker is built in (the `tsrs` crates, see "The checker"); there is no other. Structural extraction""")
rep("""`caliper-docgen extract [--tsc-path PATH]`, or `tscPath` in `docgen.config.ts` (it was `--experimental-semantic-types` until S8; `--no-checker`, or `checker: false` in the config, turns it off). `crates/semantic` asks the checker built into caliper, or with `--tsc-path` a checker binary it runs as `--api` process (see "The checker"), builds""",
    """`caliper-docgen extract` (it was `--experimental-semantic-types` until S8; `--no-checker`, or `checker: false` in the config, turns it off). `crates/semantic` asks the checker built into caliper (see "The checker"), builds""")
rep("""- **Fallback:** a missing, unsupported-version, crashed or timed-out `tsc` gives the structural result plus one `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` warning, never an error.""",
    """- **Fallback:** a checker that cannot start or does not answer in time gives the structural result plus one `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` warning, never an error.""")
rep("""- **Tests:** `crates/semantic/tests/replay.rs` runs the backend against `replay-tsc`, which answers from a recording of the real `7.1.0-beta` (`tests/fixtures/recording.json`, refreshed by `cargo run -p caliper-docgen-semantic --example record_fixture -- <typescript package dir>`; the `markers` fixture project, for names and parameters, records to `tests/fixtures/markers.recording.json` with the fixture name as a second argument; the `errors` fixture records the error type); a request the recording lacks fails the test. Fallbacks (no `tsc`, unsupported version, bad path, crash, hang) are asserted as the structural output plus one warning. The CLI test asserts the default output has no `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` diagnostic.""",
    """- **Tests:** `crates/semantic/tests/resolve.rs` runs the backend end to end against the built-in checker (the `markers` fixture project for names and parameters, `tsrs_real.rs` for the error type), and asserts a checker that does not answer in time as the structural output plus one warning. Until trail 369 slice 4 these tests replayed recordings of the Go checker through a fake `tsc` process; with the checker linked in, they ask it directly, and parity with the Go checker is `construct:parity`'s (`apps/oracle/construct-suite/README.md`). The CLI test asserts the default output has no `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` diagnostic.""")
rep("""Every program holds every root file, so either answers a component as one program would; the Storybook session and a checker process ask one; `Session::handle_request` is the dispatcher the `tsrs` binary serves, so `rpc.rs` sends the same methods and JSON over either route.""",
    """Every program holds every root file, so either answers a component as one program would; the Storybook session asks one; `Session::handle_request` is the dispatcher the `tsrs` binary serves, so `rpc.rs` sends the methods and JSON of `tsc --api`.""")
rep("""- **Lib files.** The crates embed TypeScript's lib, so a lib declaration's file is `bundled:///libs/lib.dom.d.ts` where a process names the file in its install. The path classifiers read the file name (`lib.*.d.ts`), so both are the lib (`tests/tsrs_real.rs`).
- **Same diagnostics.** A checker thread that cannot start, a request past its deadline and a stopped checker give the `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` warning the process route gives.

`--tsc-path` (or `tscPath`) runs a checker binary as an `--api` process instead, through `crates/tsc-client`, and must exist; this is how the Go `typescript` beta runs as the oracle and the parity gate (`CALIPER_TEST_TSC` in the tests, `TSRS_BIN` in the checker lane). Two packages provide one:

- **`typescript`** from 7.1 on (`7.1.0-beta`, rc and stable): `node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc`.
- **`tsrs`** (`oxc-project/tsrs`): `node_modules/tsrs/bin/tsrs`, a Node shim that starts the platform binary from `@tsrs/<platform>`, which can be given directly too. Traced on the wire against `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`: the same method sequence and the same results as `typescript@7.1.0-beta` on three recordings.

**Version rule** (`crates/tsc-client/src/supervisor.rs`, list in `crates/semantic/src/lib.rs`, `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS`). The version is read from the `package.json` of the package that owns the binary: the parent of `bin` for `typescript/bin/tsc` and `tsrs/bin/tsrs`, the binary's own directory for `@tsrs/<platform>/tsrs`. An entry is an exact version or a `major.minor` series. A `tsrs` version reads `<tsrs version>-ts<typescript version>`; it is accepted only when it is listed exactly (today `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, the build that was traced) and its TypeScript part is also taken by a TypeScript entry (`7.1`). A new `tsrs` release is therefore refused until someone traces it and adds it, as for any other build.

The protocol detail that matters for `tsrs` is unchanged from `typescript`: the client sends `createPrograms[].compilerOptions` (the Node client sends `options`; the server accepts both, and `crates/semantic/tests/replay.rs` pins the key). The tests that ask a real checker (`tsrs_real`, `cases`, `families`, `declared`, `memo`, `exports`, `composes`, `instantiate`, `watch`, and `on_demand`'s real-checker tests) ask the built-in one; `TSRS_BIN` (a `tsrs` binary) or `CALIPER_TEST_TSC` (the Go `bin/tsc`, for `instantiate`, `watch`, `composes` and `on_demand`) runs them on that process instead. Replay tests stay on the process route: handles are numbered process-wide, so a recording does not replay in a second in-process session.""",
    """- **Lib files.** The crates embed TypeScript's lib, so a lib declaration's file is `bundled:///libs/lib.dom.d.ts`. The path classifiers read the file name (`lib.*.d.ts`), so it is the lib (`tests/tsrs_real.rs`).
- **Failures.** A checker thread that cannot start, a request past its deadline and a stopped checker give one `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` warning.
- **One checker.** The product has no other route: `--tsc-path` (`tscPath`), which ran a `tsc --api` binary as a process through `crates/tsc-client`, and the version allow-list it was checked against were removed in trail 369 slice 4 (the "Spawn the tsrs binary" alternative of ADR 0026 stays rejected). The Go `typescript@7.1.0-beta` runs only in `apps/oracle`, as the oracle, the construct goldens and `construct:parity`, which compares it with the npm `tsrs` of the same release as the pinned crates (`scripts/check-packaging.mjs` holds the two pins equal).

The client sends `createPrograms[].compilerOptions` (the Node client sends `options`; the server accepts both, and `crates/semantic/tests/resolve.rs` pins the key). Every test that asks a checker (`resolve`, `tsrs_real`, `cases`, `families`, `declared`, `memo`, `exports`, `composes`, `instantiate`, `watch`, `on_demand`) asks the built-in one.""")
rep("""`caliper-docgen-semantic` keeps one checker warm (the built-in one, or a `tscPath` process) behind a worker thread,""",
    """`caliper-docgen-semantic` keeps one checker warm behind a worker thread,""")
rep("""The in-memory cache, the 64-program process replacement and the failure modes are in the ADR.""",
    """The in-memory cache, the 64-program replacement and the failure modes are in the ADR. (These numbers were measured over the `tsc --api` pipe, before the checker was linked in.)""")
rep("""- **Versions:** `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS` is the `7.1` series (`7.1.0-beta`, rc and stable releases), not one pinned build. A supervisor entry is an exact version or a `major.minor` series; `7.10.0` is not `7.1`. The protocol has no version handshake, so the `package.json` version plus the initialize call that follows the spawn are the check; a build that fails either gives the structural result and one warning. Moving past 7.1 means re-tracing the protocol.
- **Memory:** after every fourth request, once the reply is sent, the worker reads a checker process's resident memory (`/proc`, else `ps`) and replaces the process past `OnDemandConfig::max_rss_mib` (768 MiB; single-component programs peak at 157 to 612). The bound is between requests: one request that needs more finishes first. The 64-program replacement stays: every request counts as a program, whether it built a snapshot or brought the kept one up to date, and a replaced checker takes its snapshot with it. The built-in checker is replaced by a fresh session after the same 64 programs, but that does not return its memory: the allocator keeps it for this process, and the memory bound is not applied to it, since this process's resident memory is the host's (Node, Storybook) as well. Trail 369's slice 2 adds the bound for it (past it, the structural answer with a diagnostic).
- **Start and stop:** creating the checker and `warm_up` return at once, a missing `tscPath` binary answers the first request with the structural result and one diagnostic, and dropping the checker waits at most `shutdown_wait` (5 s) for a request in progress before letting the worker finish alone. The built-in checker's thread finishes a request in progress, then closes its session and exits.
- **Tests:** the tests against the real checker (`crates/semantic/tests/on_demand.rs`) ask the built-in one, and the Go `typescript-beta` with `CALIPER_TEST_TSC`, which CI sets to `apps/oracle`'s.""",
    """- **Versions:** the checker is the pinned `tsrs` crates; nothing is read from the project.
- **Memory:** the checker is replaced by a fresh session after 64 programs: every request counts as a program, whether it built a snapshot or brought the kept one up to date, and a replaced checker takes its snapshot with it. That does not return its memory: the allocator keeps it for this process, which is the host's (Node, Storybook) as well. Trail 369's slice 2 adds a bound for it (past it, the structural answer with a diagnostic).
- **Start and stop:** creating the checker and `warm_up` return at once, and dropping the checker waits at most `shutdown_wait` (5 s) for a request in progress before letting the worker finish alone. The checker's thread finishes a request in progress, then closes its session and exits.
- **Tests:** `crates/semantic/tests/on_demand.rs` asks the built-in checker.""")
save()

A union's written member order: members come sorted. The declarations of a property mapped from a property that is itself mapped over a generic instantiation (`Pick<ActionButtonProps, 'isDisabled'>` in Spectrum's generic `ActionMenu`): it has none, so it has no `parent`. A default written as a parameter's initializer.
- **`parent`** keeps react-docgen-typescript's meaning, which the structural pass shares: the interface the prop's first declaration is a member of, by name, with the file as the program read it (`getSourceFileNames`, so the case is the disk's). A member of a type literal, inline or behind an alias, has none. A property a mapped type or intersection made is asked about through its declarations, so `Pick<Base, 'p'>` gives `Base`. **`declarations`** is the interface of each declaration that is in one, the first being `parent`.
- **Tags** are keyed as the structural pass keys them (by name, the last repeated tag winning, `@param x` as `param:x`); the merge keeps the structural tags where the checker has none, as for the description. `@types/react`'s props are not asked for tags or descriptions.
- **`composes`** is the `@types/react` types the props type is made of, found by declaring file as React's terminals are (S3): its bases and an intersection's members, through the project's and dependencies' own types and through `Omit`, `Pick`, `Partial`, `Required` and `Readonly` to what they apply to. A type the structural pass could not follow and the checker did is no longer listed. Only names are wanted, so an instantiation of a generic interface (`Props<string>`, which the checker gives no bases of its own) is read through the generic type it instantiates (`getTargetOfType`), whose bases name the same React types; the layers of an over-budget type keep their arguments and still cut at such an instantiation. A list is a decision: `Some([])` says the props type is made of none and replaces the structural `composes`, and `None` (a type on the way whose bases are not known, such as a union or a type parameter) keeps the structural one.

- **Gate.** The construct suite compares description, tags, default, required, `parent` and union member order on every row in both lanes (`apps/oracle/construct-suite/README.md`, "Facts").

### Defaults and union order (ADR 0026, slice S7a2)

The checker has no parameter initializer and returns a union's members sorted, so these two facts come from oxc's syntax, read from the files the checker's answer names (`crates/core/src/types/semantic/syntax.rs`), each file once per merge. One function decides each fact in the merge: `default_of` and `declared_order` (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs`).

- **Default.** The component's code default for the prop, found by the extractor's own defaults code (`extractor/defaults.rs`, `defaultProps`) on the component's file, matched by display name and exports; else the checker's `@default` or `@defaultValue` tag; else the structural default. The code wins over the tag, as in react-docgen-typescript.
- **Union order.** The union the prop's declaration writes (`crates/core/src/extractor/written.rs`): the member of its `parent` interface in `parent.fileName`, or for a prop with no parent (a type literal), a type literal member of the component's file that is shown to be (part of) its props type: the body of the module-level alias the component's declaration names (or a member of the intersection or union that body is), or a type literal written in the component's declaration outside any body. A type literal elsewhere in the file (an imported props type with a local look-alike) says nothing. A same-file non-generic alias or enum it names is flattened in place, only where it is the declaration in scope: a type parameter, or a type an enclosing namespace, function or block declares, shadows it and the name stays as written. Each alias is flattened once per file, in the module scope, a member stated twice counts once, and a union stating more than 1,024 members through its aliases is not read (a `MAX_DEPTH_EXCEEDED` info diagnostic names the file). A member is matched by what it states (a literal, a keyword, a name it answers to), or by its kind when the written union has one member of that kind (a function, an object literal, an intersection, a template). Where it places every member, its order is used. Where it places some, the structural union's order is used if the structural union placed any member (even when that order is the checker's own), else the placed members come first in written order and the rest follow in the checker's order. Only the top-level union is ordered; a union nested in an object, array or function keeps the structural order where there is one.
- **What oxc alone cannot see.** A union whose members come through an import (`xChannel?: ColorChannel`, `Placement`): following it needs module resolution, which the resolver or the checker has, so the members stay in the checker's order (by kind, then value: not alphabetical, and not marked). A type literal declared in another file than the component's (it has no `parent` to find it by). A `@default` on a prop mapped through `Omit` or `Pick` of an instantiated generic (Spectrum's `Popover` `placement`): the checker gives it no declaration, so no tags. Code defaults the extractor does not read: `defaultProps` assigned in another module or from a variable, spread or computed defaults, and defaults applied inside a hook (`mergeProps`).
- **Switch.** `extract --no-resolver-facts` (hidden, test-only; `ResolverFacts::Off`) makes the merge take neither fact from the structural answer; the construct suite's checker lane runs with it. S7b extends it to the other facts.
- **Measured** (`extract` with the checker, then behind `--experimental-semantic-types`, with the weekly's options, tsrs `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, against the run before this slice). Before, the structural answer gave the order of 2,736 of Spectrum's 3,194 merged union props and 187 of gate-large's 432,813, and every default: on Spectrum 870 from code, 378 `@default` tags the checker also gives, 15 from the resolver only; on gate-large 499 tags. Now, Spectrum: 27 props gain a code default and none loses one; 11 of 3,686 unions change order, each to the written one (`focusMode?: 'child' | 'cell'`, `slot?: string | null`). With `--no-resolver-facts` 15 defaults (the mapped `@default` case above) and 22 more union orders (imported aliases) differ. gate-large: 834 props gain a default (the checker's `@default` tags of props only the checker returns) and none loses one; 1,452 of 432,690 unions take the written order (`translate?: 'yes' | 'no'`, `css`); with `--no-resolver-facts` no default and 16 more union orders differ (members through an import, such as MUI's `timeout?: TransitionProps['timeout'] | 'auto'`).
- **Cost.** Reading and parsing the files: 0.8 to 1.0 ms of Chakra's `Button` first answer (about 470 ms), whose union props are declared in 83 KB of Chakra's `system.gen.d.ts` and @types/react's 183 KB `index.d.ts`. On gate-large, peak RSS 610 to 616 MB against 608 to 612, and the same CPU time (two runs each).
- **Gate.** Both lanes compare `default` and member order on every row; the checker lane runs with `--no-resolver-facts` and passes every row. Rows `objects/41` to `43` (a destructured default, `defaultProps`, a code default over a different `@default`) and `literals/35` (a type literal's union) cover what a single-file row can; a union through an import needs the cross-file rows of S7b.

### The checker is the default (ADR 0026, slice S8)

The owner's decision (2026-11-12): the checker answers by default on every surface, the whole-project `extract` included, though its default no longer has the structural resolver's speed. One name per concept: `--no-checker` on the command line, `checker: false` in `docgen.config.ts`, the napi options and the Storybook addon. `--experimental-semantic-types`, the config's `experimentalSemanticTypes` and `semanticTypes` are removed: the CLI and the config refuse them as unknown, and the addon refuses `semanticTypes` by name, since left unread `semanticTypes: 'off'` would quietly run the checker.

- **CLI.** `extract` and `check` wait for the checker over every component, `inspect` for the one it shows. `--tsc-path`, `--semantic-timeout-ms` and the test-only `--no-resolver-facts` conflict with `--no-checker`. `watch` stays structural (its help says so), and warns only when the config names a `tscPath` it will not run.
- **napi and the addon.** A session attaches the warm checker unless `checker: false`, and keeps ADR 0022: the structural answer first, the checker's within `semanticWaitMs` (150 ms), the addon's `prefetchStories` paying the wait of the opening story. `extractAll` stays structural.
- **Vite plugin.** It has no switch and serves the whole output as one module and every transformed file's docs at once, which no checker wait fits, so it creates its session with `checker: false`.
- **Measurement.** The construct suite's structural lane passes `--no-checker`: its expectations are the resolver's. `scripts/weekly.py` (its time, memory, recall and oracle runs), `scripts/agent_eval.py` and `just bench` run the default, the checker, and the weekly's per-corpus budgets are "record on first run" (`docs/measurement.md`, "The budgets"). The checker lane, which held the checker path before, now runs the default with `--tsc-path`.
- **Cost.** `extract` of `gate-large` (938 Chakra and MUI wrappers): 6.05 s and about 970 MiB by default, 0.10 s and 200 MiB with `--no-checker`; three copies of it (2,814 components) 15.4 s and 1,053 MiB. A lazy session asked for all 938 peaks at 1,058 MiB with the checker against 377 MiB without, once the kept answers share their props (before, about 6.7 MiB per Chakra component, 2.6 GB at 300). The record is [gate measurements](gate-measurements.md#the-checker-is-the-default-s8).
- **Tests.** `crates/cli/tests/commands.rs` holds the default against `--no-checker` on a prop only the checker evaluates (`ReturnType<typeof make>`) for `extract` and `inspect`, and the napi binding's and the addon's tests hold that a session asks the checker unless told not to.

Two beta behaviors to know: the server panics (`interface conversion: interface {} is string, not float64`) when `createProgram` gets string-valued enum options such as `target: 'es2022'`, so pass options from `parseConfigFile`; and `true`/`false` literal types carry neither `value` nor `intrinsicName`, so read them with `typeToString`. Discovery over a whole project ran in the oracle: 33 to 1,531 components per corpus.
51:| 55-file corpus, one program | 385 ms and 937 requests. RDT in-process: 955 ms |
55:Trimming the process, on the MUI `Button` query (median of 5 runs, 2026-09-20). Differences under about 10 ms are noise.
70:- **Backend crate** (`crates/semantic`, always compiled in and enabled at run time, ADR 0007) spawns `tsc --api` through `crates/tsc-client`, runs the algorithm, and handles timeouts. Core never depends on it: the CLI runs the backend and calls core's `merge_semantic`.
81:| Lifecycle | Client built and tested against a fake tsc and the real nightly (`crates/tsc-client`): missing binary, unsupported version, timeout, crash, malformed or oversized frame, partial project failure, shutdown reaping, stale notification. The supervisor does not restart a crashed `tsc`: a session that ends stays ended, and `OnDemand` in `crates/semantic` respawns it, at most three times, and its replay test covers a crash falling back with one diagnostic. Open: header-size cap, stderr that isn't UTF-8, honoring `handshake_timeout` |

## Boundaries

- **`crates/core`** owns the semantic result type, the merge and the diagnostics. It has no I/O, no async and no protocol types. The merge lives here because `OpaqueDetail` and `ParsedProp` internals are `pub(crate)`.
- **Backend crate** (`crates/semantic`, always compiled in and enabled at run time, ADR 0007) spawns `tsc --api` through `crates/tsc-client`, runs the algorithm, and handles timeouts. Core never depends on it: the CLI runs the backend and calls core's `merge_semantic`.
- **CLI and NAPI** run it by default and turn it off on request. Neither calls JS.
- **Cold path only.** The hook is synchronous and runs on the cold path; `WatchSession::update_file` does not run it.
- **Failure** leaves the structural result and adds a diagnostic. It never fails extraction.
- **Determinism.** Reversing the query order changed no union order across 16 props in 3 files (2026-09-20). Whether canonical output sorts unions is open (below).

| Determinism | Clean and incremental runs must produce the same output |
| Oracle | Fixed. See below |

## The RDT oracle

`apps/oracle` depends on TypeScript 7.1 directly (for the oracle), but RDT 2.4.0 crashes on import against it (`ts.JsxEmit` is undefined). The removed harness's `compare.ts`/`analyze.ts` (caliper-docgen vs RDT/react-docgen) compared only name, `required`, type and default, and rendered our types themselves in `run-ours.ts` (objects print as `{ ... }`), so their type mismatches mixed resolver and renderer differences. Those limits went with it: `scripts/weekly.py` compares Caliper's own and `@types/react` props with RDT's by name, and the oracle compares prop types structurally against the TS 7.1 checker (`docs/measurement.md`).

# 0026. The checker is the type authority; oxc supplies syntax

**Status:** Accepted (2026-11-08) **Date:** 2026-11-07

## Context

ADR 0006 and 0007 made the TypeScript checker an opt-in second resolver, because a whole-project `tsc` run cost up to 9.3 s and 975 MiB (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`); ADR 0022 bounded it to a warm per-component request. The structural default still answers wrong without a marker: a type that is only a call signature becomes `{}`, `Omit`, `Pick` and `Partial` reached through an alias lose their effect, and a factory's props are taken from a name-matched interface (`docs/rdt-differences.md`, classes 4 to 6). A prototype found more: `[string, ...number[]]` prints as `[string, number[][]]` and a getter reads as a method. Each fix is another rule in a resolver that re-implements the type system.

tsrs (`oxc-project/tsrs`, Apache-2.0) is a Rust port of the TypeScript 7 checker at microsoft/TypeScript `3e9236361fa9`, the commit `typescript@7.1.0-beta` was built from. It speaks the same `--api` protocol: the 19 methods caliper calls are all present, and 87 one-prop fixtures got the same oracle verdicts as `typescript-beta`. A throwaway prototype through the Node client (not in the repository; these numbers are the record) measured on Chakra `ButtonProps` (1,138 props) a 43-47 ms snapshot and the first converted prop at 62-67 ms, where ADR 0022 measured 703 ms with `tsc` on a different program root (indicative, not an A/B), with tsrs peaking at 126-130 MiB. On 16 hand-written components the checker was equal or better on 14, worse on union member order and an unresolvable import. A polymorphic component instantiated through a virtual file gave 267 props for `'div'` where both engines give 2 today. tsrs's own benchmark (`bench/RESULTS.md`) reports 1.8 to 4.2 times TypeScript 7.1 beta's speed and 2.1 to 2.6 times less memory.

## Decision

The checker decides types and oxc decides syntax.

- **Authority.** The checker is the default source of a component's prop set, each prop's type, requiredness and description. oxc supplies candidate components (`extractor/evidence.rs`, `uses.rs`), defaults, JSDoc positions, source locations and declaration order, which is re-applied to union members because the checker sorts them by flags and value.
- **One projection model.** Checker facts convert once into the canonical model. Canonical JSON, TOON and the RDT view are projections of it, and no projection makes a type decision.
- **Fallback.** The structural resolver stays only for when the checker cannot answer: not installed or offline, an unsupported platform, a crash, a timeout. Its types carry `degradedBy` and the run carries one diagnostic.
- **Opt-out.** The checker runs unless `--no-checker` (`checker: false` in the config, the napi binding and the Storybook addon) turns it off; `--experimental-semantic-types` and `semanticTypes` are removed (S8).
- **Per surface.** The Storybook addon keeps ADR 0022: the structural answer first, the checker's within `semanticWaitMs`. Its premise that the checker is too slow for first paint was re-measured with tsrs in S4 and holds (Chakra's `Button`, 562 ms, 402 ms after the first-answer work). The CLI and agents wait for the checker, all candidates in one snapshot, with a timeout (10 s proposed).
- **Pin.** We pin exact tsrs crates (`tsrs_api` and `tsrs_vfs` `=0.24.0`, TypeScript `3e9236361fa9`) and bump them on purpose; the checker lane's `tsrs` binary (`0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, the same TypeScript commit) follows them. A bump passes the deterministic construct suite (`apps/oracle/construct-suite`, being built on `feat/construct-suite`) and a tsrs-against-Go parity run of it. The weekly oracle keeps the Go `typescript` checker: an oracle running the checker that produced the answer agrees with it by construction.
- **Linked.** The product links the tsrs crates and asks `tsrs_api::Session` in process, on one thread with a 512 MiB stack, the stack the `tsrs` binary serves on; nothing is installed. `--tsc-path` (`tscPath`) runs a checker binary as a process instead, which is how the Go `typescript` beta stays the oracle and the parity gate. A checker process is replaced above an RSS threshold (`OnDemandConfig::max_rss_mib`); the linked checker is replaced by a fresh session after 64 programs, which does not return its memory.
- **Collapsed React types.** `ReactElement`, `JSX.Element` and `ReactChild` stay collapsed to the `reactNode` terminal. No evaluation showed it hurting Storybook controls.

Linked rather than spawned (trail 369): the crates are published (0.24.0), the same recorded Chakra answer (3,776 requests) takes 141 ms in process against 367 ms over the pipe with equal answers, and there is no per-platform binary to ship or find. What it costs: a stack overflow inside the checker aborts the host process (the 512 MiB thread holds a type 10,000 deep), a dropped session does not return its memory (trail 369 slice 2 bounds it, then answers structurally), and each linked artifact grows by about 22 MB.

## Consequences

- Supersedes "structural stays the default" in ADR 0006 and 0007 and 0007's "never a silent default" trigger. The rest of both stands.
- Deletable or shrinkable with a thin fallback, estimated from each file's header: in `crates/core/src/resolver`, `alias`, `chain`, `evaluate`, `substitute`, `named`, `primitives`, `extends`, `func`, `template`, `import`, `callee`, `memo`, `deps`, `collected` and `precedence` shrink to a no-generics subset and `mod.rs` by half; `dependency_types.rs` and `import_map.rs` go (the checker resolves modules; ADR 0010 and 0025 narrow to the fallback); in `extractor`, `interface` (but cva), `alias`, `values`, `reexports`, `asserted` and most of `visit` go, and `component`, `wrapper` and `mod.rs` shrink to candidate detection. About 7,600 of 25,300 non-test lines, 9,400 with no fallback, which Windows ARM64 rules out. `html`, `react`, `ambient`, `evidence`, `uses`, `defaults` and `jsdoc` stay; `crates/semantic` and `crates/tsc-client` grow and `convert.rs` is rewritten.
- Contract: `PropType` gains what the checker knows and it cannot hold: tuple element optional, rest and labels, `bigint`, `unique symbol`, enum identity, template literals, overload sets, call signatures on objects, a recursion marker, and a typed truncation in place of `Named` with checker text. React terminals (`ReactNode`, `CSSProperties`, `Ref`, `ElementType`, HTML attributes) are recognized by declaring path, as `is_react_declared` (`crates/semantic/src/component.rs`) does. `SCHEMA_VERSION` and `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump (ADR 0017).
- No cache is keyed on a type id: ids are per checker and change with query order. Keys are file content, export name, instantiation and the tsrs pin. The checker does not see an edit it is not told about, so watch forwards every change.
- Unsolved: a per-component dependency closure from the checker (invalidation stays conservative), and the structural answer's gaps wherever the fallback runs.
- Risks: tsrs is pre-1.0, four releases in twelve days, and closed to pull requests (its README). Memory grew from 98 to 246 MB over 150 Chakra edits with each old snapshot disposed (#920 and #646 open). Determinism across checker counts is shown only on a 72-file program. There is no `@tsrs/win32-arm64` package, so those users get the fallback. The linked crates add about 22 MB to the CLI and to the napi binding.

Migration, each slice behind a deterministic gate, none on the oracle. The tsrs backend (the Rust client running on tsrs, PR 390) is done.

1. **S1** (done) Shared projection model and the new `PropType` variants, filled by the structural path where it knows them. Gate: a unit test per variant, golden JSON diff, cache schema test.
2. **S2** (done) Flag-based converter in `convert.rs`, memoized by type id within one snapshot, with a named-boundary policy and caps. Gate: the construct suite's expected JSON; reversed query order gives identical bytes.
3. **S3** (done) React terminals by declaring path. Gate: no regression against today's Chakra `Button` terminals.
4. **S4** (done, one gate failed) The checker's answer wins when it runs: the addon inside ADR 0022's window, the CLI waiting (`--semantic-timeout-ms`, 10 s), and a prop the checker could not read keeps its structural type with `degradedBy` (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`). Gate: checker-on output equals structural on the suite except a listed set of improvements (held by the checker lane); Chakra first answer at most 150 ms through the Rust client (measured 562 ms, then 402 ms once each answer was parsed once and a type's parts asked for once; FAIL: the floor of that request set with no round trips is about 230 ms, 81% of its bytes the property lists of Chakra's style-prop condition maps, so the seam has to change rather than the budget: [gate measurements](../gate-measurements.md#first-answer-s4), and ADR 0022's structural-first answer stands); the Storybook harness re-run (not run: it needs the corpora).
5. **S5** (done) Instantiation of generic and polymorphic components through a virtual file: a component whose first type parameter declares a default is read at it, from a file the checker holds in memory (`createSnapshot`'s `fileSystem` layer, read by tsrs and the Go beta alike) in a second snapshot made only when a requested component is generic; an instantiation that does not form keeps the structural props with the checker's error as the reason ([generic components](../type-checker-integration.md#generic-components-adr-0026-slice-s5)). Gate: `Poly<'div'>` gives at least 260 props and `'a'` differs (PASS: 281 and 289, on tsrs and the Go checker, `crates/semantic/tests/instantiate.rs`).
6. **S6** (done, one gate failed) Watch on `snapshot.update` with RSS recycling: the warm checker keeps its snapshot and brings it up to date with `updateSnapshot` (`ensurePrograms`, the files the session announced), and before an answer compares every file its program read with the stamp it had; an unannounced change answers from a fresh snapshot with a warning naming the file ([watch](../type-checker-integration.md#watch-adr-0026-slice-s6)). # 0026. The checker is the type authority; oxc supplies syntax

**Status:** Accepted (2026-11-08) **Date:** 2026-11-07

## Context

ADR 0006 and 0007 made the TypeScript checker an opt-in second resolver, because a whole-project `tsc` run cost up to 9.3 s and 975 MiB (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`); ADR 0022 bounded it to a warm per-component request. The structural default still answers wrong without a marker: a type that is only a call signature becomes `{}`, `Omit`, `Pick` and `Partial` reached through an alias lose their effect, and a factory's props are taken from a name-matched interface (`docs/rdt-differences.md`, classes 4 to 6). A prototype found more: `[string, ...number[]]` prints as `[string, number[][]]` and a getter reads as a method. Each fix is another rule in a resolver that re-implements the type system.

tsrs (`oxc-project/tsrs`, Apache-2.0) is a Rust port of the TypeScript 7 checker at microsoft/TypeScript `3e9236361fa9`, the commit `typescript@7.1.0-beta` was built from. It speaks the same `--api` protocol: the 19 methods caliper calls are all present, and 87 one-prop fixtures got the same oracle verdicts as `typescript-beta`. A throwaway prototype through the Node client (not in the repository; these numbers are the record) measured on Chakra `ButtonProps` (1,138 props) a 43-47 ms snapshot and the first converted prop at 62-67 ms, where ADR 0022 measured 703 ms with `tsc` on a different program root (indicative, not an A/B), with tsrs peaking at 126-130 MiB. On 16 hand-written components the checker was equal or better on 14, worse on union member order and an unresolvable import. A polymorphic component instantiated through a virtual file gave 267 props for `'div'` where both engines give 2 today. tsrs's own benchmark (`bench/RESULTS.md`) reports 1.8 to 4.2 times TypeScript 7.1 beta's speed and 2.1 to 2.6 times less memory.

## Decision

The checker decides types and oxc decides syntax.

- **Authority.** The checker is the default source of a component's prop set, each prop's type, requiredness and description. oxc supplies candidate components (`extractor/evidence.rs`, `uses.rs`), defaults, JSDoc positions, source locations and declaration order, which is re-applied to union members because the checker sorts them by flags and value.
- **One projection model.** Checker facts convert once into the canonical model. Canonical JSON, TOON and the RDT view are projections of it, and no projection makes a type decision.
- **Fallback.** The structural resolver stays only for when the checker cannot answer: not installed or offline, an unsupported platform, a crash, a timeout. Its types carry `degradedBy` and the run carries one diagnostic.
- **Opt-out.** The checker runs unless `--no-checker` (`checker: false` in the config, the napi binding and the Storybook addon) turns it off; `--experimental-semantic-types` and `semanticTypes` are removed (S8).
- **Per surface.** The Storybook addon keeps ADR 0022: the structural answer first, the checker's within `semanticWaitMs`. Its premise that the checker is too slow for first paint was re-measured with tsrs in S4 and holds (Chakra's `Button`, 562 ms, 402 ms after the first-answer work). The CLI and agents wait for the checker, all candidates in one snapshot, with a timeout (10 s proposed).
- **Pin.** We pin exact tsrs crates (`tsrs_api` and `tsrs_vfs` `=0.24.0`, TypeScript `3e9236361fa9`) and bump them on purpose; the checker lane's `tsrs` binary (`0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, the same TypeScript commit) follows them. A bump passes the deterministic construct suite (`apps/oracle/construct-suite`, being built on `feat/construct-suite`) and a tsrs-against-Go parity run of it. The weekly oracle keeps the Go `typescript` checker: an oracle running the checker that produced the answer agrees with it by construction.
- **Linked.** The product links the tsrs crates and asks `tsrs_api::Session` in process, on one thread with a 512 MiB stack, the stack the `tsrs` binary serves on; nothing is installed. `--tsc-path` (`tscPath`) runs a checker binary as a process instead, which is how the Go `typescript` beta stays the oracle and the parity gate. ## Known gaps of the structural resolver (the fallback, and `--no-checker`)

See the "Known gaps summary" table in `rdt-coverage.md` for the full, maintained list. The short version: conditional types that need inference (`infer`, an unbound generic), mapped types over an unbound generic, and a couple of `@emotion/styled`-specific call shapes all need real type inference OXC deliberately doesn't do: the checker, on by default, answers them. Not bugs. A conditional, indexed access or mapped type whose operands are known is evaluated (`resolver/evaluate.rs`).

**The TypeScript checker is the default** (ADR 0026, S8 done 2026-11-12). `extract`, `check` and `inspect` merge the built-in checker's answer (the `tsrs` crates; `--tsc-path` runs a binary instead) over the structural one prop by prop, napi sessions and the Storybook addon ask it per component within `semanticWaitMs` (ADR 0022), and `--no-checker` (`checker: false`) turns it off; `watch` and the Vite plugin stay structural. A prop the checker could not read keeps the structural type with `degradedBy`, and a failed, crashed or timed-out checker falls back to the structural result with one warning. The gates before the flip (checker lane, determinism, Linux CI, memory past 600 edits, tsrs-against-Go parity) are recorded in ADR 0026. It began as the opt-in slice 1 (ADR 0006, ADR 0007, `type-checker-integration.md`), whose accuracy was verified against real RDT: 0 missing/extra props on 13 hand-picked components, and on `7.1.0-beta` against the full 44-file fixture corpus (5,508/5,522 `required` matches, 5,266/5,522 type-string matches). TypeScript 7.1's Go checker also runs, test-only, as an oracle for structural prop types (`docs/measurement.md`); the weekly record measures the checker, the default (`oracle.universe_version` 5).

## Experiments that didn't pan out

**Confidence routing (2026-10-25).** The idea: score each component's risk of wrong or missing props from Caliper's own output, and ask the TypeScript 7.1 checker only about the risky ones. Measured against the checker on 518,268 shared props over the five corpora and the fixtures, routing 10% of components caught 23% of the props only the checker reports with the existing warning rule (a component with a degrade warning or error), against 3% for a smoothed table and 6% for a logistic model. At a 20% budget neither model caught the one prop the oracle marks `wrong`. Most of the checker-only props were Next's ambient augmentation or false component matches, which a score of structural risk can't learn (the 1,154 of 1,182 on shadcn quoted then came from a run that no longer reproduces: the weekly record of 2026-11-06 finds 55 checker-only props on shadcn, all `tw`, and `docs/rdt-differences.md` has the current account). So no score ships: warnings stay the signal, and on-demand checker use asks about the requested component instead of predicting. The script was deleted, so the routing numbers above cannot be reproduced; the method is the oracle in `docs/measurement.md`.
# Fail CI on extraction errors (--strict also fails on warnings)
caliper-docgen check --src src
```

`extract`, `check` and `inspect` ask the checker; `--no-checker` (config `checker: false`) skips it, and `--tsc-path` runs a checker binary instead (`typescript@7.1`'s `tsc`, or `tsrs`). Settings can also live in a `docgen.config.ts` (`srcDirs`, `htmlAttributes`, `cacheDir`, `checker`, and more). `caliper-docgen --help` lists the rest, including `schema` for the JSON Schema of the output.

Parsed declarations and the dependency index are cached under `node_modules/.cache/caliper-docgen`. `--no-cache` (config, NAPI, Vite and Storybook option `cache: false`) reads and writes nothing there; the output is the same.

```

`crates/core` has no dependency on async runtimes, NAPI, or terminal libraries. It can be linked from any host. It does read and write files itself: source discovery, module resolution, the parse and dependency caches (`cache.rs`, `dependency_types.rs`) and tsconfig lookups. It never spawns a process; the checker backend that does lives in `crates/semantic`. `crates/semantic` and `crates/tsc-client` are published crates, always compiled into the CLI and the binding and enabled at run time (ADR 0007); Callisto publishes them before the CLI.

## Module layout
  completions.rs  — shell completion generation
```

### `crates/semantic/src/` and `crates/tsc-client/src/`

`semantic` is the TypeScript 7.1 checker backend, on by default: `lib.rs` (the whole-project run), `on_demand.rs` (a warm checker that answers one component at a time), `checker.rs` (the built-in `tsrs` checker, or a `--tsc-path` process), `component.rs`, `convert.rs`, `locate.rs` (checks an explicit checker binary) and `rpc.rs` (typed calls over one checker session). `tsc-client` is the process supervisor and JSON-RPC transport under it.

## Key types

### `CollectedType` — raw structural type from the extractor

- `crates/cli` — clap CLI, no logic; @crates/cli/AGENTS.md
- `crates/binding` — thin NAPI wrapper, delegates to core
- `crates/semantic` — TypeScript 7.1 checker backend, on by default (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`)
- `crates/tsc-client` — client for the checker process the semantic crate drives

## Scripts
- 19. Load dependency declarations by default — removed: a default, with its measurements. It lives in `docs/performance.md` ("Default changes").
- 20. Chain dependency layers and load the remaining names after three growths — removed: a tuning of 0016's design with measurements, not a new decision. It lives in `docs/architecture/pipeline-orchestration.md` ("Demand-driven dependencies") and `docs/performance.md`. It replaced 0016's 48-growth threshold.
- 21. Publish the semantic backend crates with the CLI — removed: a release procedure. Callisto publishes `caliper-docgen-tsc-client` and `caliper-docgen-semantic` before the CLI (`callisto.toml`, `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`); 0007's always-compiled backend is why they are public crates.
- [22. Ask a warm checker for the requested component](0022-ask-a-warm-checker-for-the-requested-component.md) — do not route by predicted risk or check the whole project to answer one story: ask the TypeScript checker for the component a request names, wait a bounded time, and take the structural answer when it is slower. Extends 0007's runtime opt-in from a project run to a session.
- 23. Function parameters carry `optional` and `rest` — removed: a field added under 0017's versioning rule. It lives in `docs/architecture/serialization-formats.md` ("Version 3").
## What a release produces

| Output | Where | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Crates | crates.io | `caliper-docgen-core`, `-tsc-client`, `-semantic`, `caliper-docgen` |
| npm packages | npm, with provenance | CLI wrapper and its four platform packages, napi binding and its platform packages, Vite plugin, Storybook addon |
| Tags | this repository | One per package, such as `cargo/caliper-docgen@x.y.z` and `npm/caliper-docgen@x.y.z` |
**Invariant 2: `htmlAttributes` never silently defaults.** `TryFrom<JsExtractOptions> for PipelineOptions` treats every `Option<T>` field as "use `PipelineOptions::default()`" when `None`, _except_ `html_attributes`, which goes through `HtmlAttributeMode::parse` and hard-errors, naming the bad value, if the caller (e.g. via a TypeScript `as any` cast bypassing the `'curated' | 'full' | 'none'` `ts_type`) passes something that isn't one of the three accepted strings. This is a deliberate application of AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 ("never fail silently") at the boundary where TypeScript's type system stops being a real guarantee.

**Invariant 3: `JsExtractOptions` carries only options the pipeline reads.** Every field of `JsExtractOptions` maps to a `PipelineOptions` field or is consumed by the binding itself when it builds a session (`lazy`, `checker`, `tscPath`, `semanticWaitMs`, `semanticWaitEmptyMs`). There are no JSON-string fields for map-valued options: no `extraPathsJson` or `knownTypeOverridesJson` exists, and neither `extraPaths` nor `knownTypeOverrides` is an option anywhere. Adding an option means adding the field here, mapping it in `TryFrom<JsExtractOptions> for PipelineOptions`, and a test that shows it changes output; an option that is accepted but not read lets a caller believe it is honored.

## Session-ID scheme (LOCKED DESIGN DECISION, with an accepted gap)
- `scripts/gate_fixtures.mjs` installs `@chakra-ui/react` 3.37.0 and `@mui/material` 9.5.0 (the root `package.json`'s pins) with `pnpm`, and writes one wrapper per exported component, `export function ChakraButton(props: ComponentProps<typeof Button>)`: 1,616 components (1,466 Chakra, 150 MUI). The Chakra and MUI sources themselves were not fetched, so this is not the Chakra corpus of `docs/measurement.md`: it is what an app that wraps both libraries asks the checker.
- Each request to the checker builds a program that loads one library's declarations whole, which is what makes it a large program.
- The harness uses the session a Storybook addon runs: a lazy `WatchSession` with `load_dependencies` on, nothing collapsed, and a warm `OnDemand` that waits up to 120 s, over the pinned tsrs binary the oracle's `tsrs-bin.ts` resolves.

content.content:
The experimental TypeScript checker is now built in: `--experimental-semantic-types` and `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'` use the `tsrs` checker linked into Caliper, so there is nothing to install, and a project's own `typescript` or `tsrs` is no longer looked for. It is still off by default. To run another checker, pass `--tsc-path` (or `tscPath`) a `tsc` of `typescript@7.1` or a `tsrs` binary, as before; a project that relied on its own `typescript@beta` being found must now pass it this way. The CLI binary and the native binding are each about 22 MB larger, and their npm packages carry tsrs's `NOTICE`.
8:A whole-project `extract` with the checker (the default) is about three to four times as fast, with the same output. On an app wrapping the 938 components of Chakra UI and MUI it takes 1.8 s instead of 6.2 s, and 1.4 s instead of 5.7 s for the 787 Chakra components alone; `react-docgen-typescript` takes 7.3 s and 4.1 s on the same files. The checker's answer for a prop that many components share (Chakra's style props) is now converted and merged once instead of once per component, the answers are read on several threads, and the built-in checker answers two programs over the same files at once. Peak memory is about 10% higher (1.1 GiB instead of 0.98 on that app; 1.5 GiB on three copies of it). The Storybook session and a checker run through `--tsc-path` keep asking one program.
---
cargo/caliper-docgen-semantic: minor
---

For library users: `OnDemand::recycles()` reports how many times the warm checker's process was replaced on purpose, split into `worn` (it built its 64 programs) and `bloated` (it passed `max_rss_mib`), and `OnDemand::process_id()` names the process that answered last. Replacements are also logged at debug level. Nothing changes for the CLI, the addon or the output.

+const cargo = readFileSync(join(root, 'Cargo.toml'), 'utf8')
+const npmTsrs = readJson('apps/oracle/package.json').devDependencies?.tsrs ?? ''
+const npmRelease = npmTsrs.split('-ts')[0]

+  const pin = cargo.match(new RegExp(`^${crate}\\s*=\\s*"=([^"]+)"`, 'm'))?.[1]

+  } else if (pin !== npmRelease) {
+    problems.push(
+      `Cargo.toml pins ${crate} =${pin}, but apps/oracle's tsrs is ${JSON.stringify(npmTsrs)}: construct:parity must run the release the product links`,

+  }

of the semantic backend. `crates/tsc-client` is deleted: nothing needs the

`tsc` process ask the linked checker instead, which every one of them already
did in its "real" variant; the recordings, `replay-tsc` and the

now on the npm `tsrs` of the release the product links (0.24.0), which
`scripts/check-packaging.mjs` holds equal to the Cargo pins; dependabot
leaves the tsrs pins alone. The checker lane runs the release binary's
built-in checker, so `tsrs-bin.ts` goes, and CI no longer sets
CALIPER_TEST_TSC.

Trail 369 slice 4 is pushed: `feat/delete-process-route` at ffb40a53, one signed commit on main 7e024e25. `git ls-remote` shows the same SHA. I did not open a PR or watch CI.

**Deleted** (111 files, +590/−6,487):
- The process route: the process `Client`/`Backend` variant, its supervision and the RSS replacement of a process, `locate.rs`, `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS` and the `Backend::start` path argument.
- `--tsc-path`/`tscPath` everywhere: CLI, config, napi, Storybook addon, docs, help trycmd. The config refuses `tscPath` as an unknown key; the addon refuses it by name.
- The `watch` note about ignoring `tscPath`.
- The 12 Go recordings, `replay-tsc` and `examples/record_fixture.rs`.
- The oracle's `tsrs-bin.ts` and `CALIPER_TEST_TSC` in CI.
- No `@tsrs/<platform>` packaging or project-typescript fallback was left on main.

**tsc-client is deleted entirely**, along with its workspace entry, callisto entry, semver recipe entry, two pending changesets and tokio's `process`/`io-util` features. No test needs the Go checker: recordings can't be replayed in-process, so the replay tests now ask the linked checker, which their "real" variants already did. Go parity is covered by `construct:parity`.

**Tests dropped:** the process-only cases (crash, hang, invalid JSON, missing binary, wrong version, process memory bound, a request stuck at drop). The timeout fallback is now tested in-process.

**Public API and changesets:** I added `.changeset/checker-binary-option-removed.md` with Breaking:/Action:. It bumps semantic, core, CLI and napi minor; `OnDemandConfig::max_rss_mib`, `OnDemand::process_id` and `Recycles::bloated` are among the removals. I also edited three pending changesets that mentioned `--tsc-path` or `process_id`.

**Slice 5 items:** the oracle's npm `tsrs` moves to 0.24.0 to match the crates, and `construct:parity` passes 235/235 on it. `check-packaging.mjs` now fails if the two pins differ. Dependabot ignores `tsrs_*` and `tsrs`.

**What's left of the Go beta:** only `apps/oracle` (`typescript-beta`, goldens, `construct:parity`), all unchanged. ADR 0026, type-checker-integration, STATUS, README, ARCHITECTURE, AGENTS and the release docs are updated.

**Checks, all exit 0:** `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `just deny`, `just semver` (breaks covered by the changeset), `just test-rust` (1407 passed), `just test-checker-lane` (which includes `construct:parity`), `just test-ts`, `just test-napi`, `just test-integration`. `extract --json` on gate-large is identical apart from `stats.durationMs`.

**#440 conflicts:** origin/main had not moved, so there was nothing to merge. #440 (now at c3baec49) is not merged and conflicts with this branch in 8 files: `checker.rs`, `on_demand.rs`, `gate_harness.rs`, `tests/on_demand.rs`, the ADR, `gate-measurements.md`, `type-checker-integration.md`, `justfile`. It re-adds `max_rss_mib` and process-memory code that this PR deletes. Whichever lands second should keep #440's in-process guards and drop its process branches (`Worn`/`Bloated`, `process_id`).

**Not verified:** gate-measure on the reworked harness (not run), Linux, CI.
